    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` already references `auth.users`. Today only the space pseudo-account sets it. <roam uid="f6tgGk3-t"/>
    - `upsert_account_in_space` already writes a `SpaceAccess` row for an account whose `dg_account` is set. This anticipates personal accounts with copied grants. <roam uid="umtrUcTmK"/>
  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK"/>
    - ENG-1837 adds `everyone` to it. The agent change adds the agent's principal and that principal's groups. Personal accounts would be the third change to this function. <roam uid="bUiWiBwvl"/>
  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`. An Obsidian account looks local to its vault (not verified). <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agent grants owned by a person: an agent reads what its person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
- Decision: how a personal account is linked to a platform identity <roam uid="HrW3SuczV"/>
  - **Why it matters:** anyone who holds a space password can claim to be any member of that space. This decision sets how much proof a link needs, and therefore whether a co-member can take over another member's attribution and their access to other spaces. Stronger proof costs the person effort or depends on Roam. <roam uid="G_ksAI6Q_"/>
  - The threat <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl"/>
    - Anyone with the space password can mint a claim as that space. In Roam, that is every graph member. <roam uid="3TQldEoEj"/>
    - A co-member can therefore claim another member's Roam uid and take over their attribution, and their access to other spaces if the claim spreads beyond the space. <roam uid="8miESmtZh"/>
    - Outsiders can't do this under any option below. <roam uid="EJZYtvlMR"/>
    - Example: Mallory reads graph A's space password, calls `create_secret_token` as the space with Alice's uid in the payload, opens the link, and logs in with her own Google account. `create_secret_token` accepts any payload from any authenticated caller. <roam uid="6gK3VqcE-"/>
  - Two kinds of claim <roam uid="_oWUtNrtr"/>
    - An access claim is an `asserted` claim: "I am this platform account", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have. <roam uid="qbzJP8qlz"/>
    - An identity claim says "this platform account is me". It carries attribution and may spread to other spaces, so it needs stronger proof. <roam uid="jriBBo825"/>
    - The group wants identity, not only access. <roam uid="tre8QheiL"/>
  - Verified identifiers are separate from links <roam uid="o_xM2FmbI"/>
    - A personal account can hold verified identifiers that aren't tied to any platform account: emails, Google or GitHub identities, an ORCID iD, an ATProto handle. <roam uid="rvWITqil4"/>
    - They serve login, the profile, and attribution on their own. <roam uid="cMWL7UAPb"/>
    - An identifier becomes evidence for a link only when a platform records the same identifier for a platform account. That is what L1 checks for email. <roam uid="Q1mfw83z-"/>
    - Obsidian attribution relies on these identifiers, since Obsidian rarely records anything we can check. <roam uid="dPJOYzQfI"/>
  - Email as the bridge <roam uid="WbpaSzu1V"/>
    - The Roam plugin can read `:user/email` through datalog. <roam uid="q37Xq8DVO"/>
    - If the personal account proves control of an email (Google login, or a verification mail) and Roam records that email for the uid, a forger fails: they can't log in as the victim's email. <roam uid="Zt5yx9RoU"/>
    - The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. If it comes from the claim's own payload, the forger writes their own email. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts. <roam uid="Qr1nAWi-I"/>
  - Layers <roam uid="tZGbhisXM"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the layers are the choices for the identity-link decision. Each one stops a different kind of forgery, at a different cost to the person and to us. The packages below combine them, so read those first if you only want the trade-offs. <roam uid="jY7-WynXq"/>
    - The layers stack. Each one is described by what it stops and what it costs. <roam uid="fBoQ0vuf5"/>
    - L0: Token handoff only. The plugin mints a `secret_token` with the uid; the person logs in on the Website. <roam uid="_qMYaUHJ0"/>
      - Stops outsiders only. <roam uid="ZjIn7a1og"/>
      - Burden: none. Cost: lowest, reuses the `auth/token` route. Platforms: all. <roam uid="bM5E9fXbZ"/>
    - L1: Email binding. The personal account must control the email that the platform records for the platform account. <roam uid="ShFzQ-cQE"/>
      - Control of the email can be proven two ways, both at this layer: a verification mail, or a linked external identity (Google, GitHub, ...) whose provider vouches that the email is verified. Many Roam users sign in to Roam with Google, so the same Google account often proves the match in one step. <roam uid="0ngOboLPC"/>
      - Only provider emails marked as verified count. Supabase also links identities that share a verified email automatically, so the account's set of verified emails must be read from the account, not from one login. <roam uid="L3hwsR2X1"/>
      - Stops a forger who can't also falsify the binding source. <roam uid="eNir7ER3F"/>
      - Burden: the person verifies once. Cost: low. The verification can start from any plugin or from the Website. Platforms: any platform that records an email for the account. Roam does; for Obsidian, see below. <roam uid="KgXX_YwXm"/>
      - Obsidian <roam uid="cx9aeX2_F"/>
        - The Obsidian plugin sends no email today (`email: undefined` in `supabaseContext.ts`). Whether it can read the email of the Obsidian account, and whether that email is verified, is not checked yet. Using an Obsidian account is optional, so some users have none. <roam uid="sx3sITsvn"/>
        - The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there. <roam uid="AM08ShSzs"/>
        - An email the person types in is not a platform record. Verifying it gives the personal account a verified identifier, but says nothing about which platform account is theirs. <roam uid="nvfy6pgBo"/>
        - A vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim by one of them covers the others' content too. <roam uid="vBcLpeOcv"/>
    - L2: Corroboration. Accept the binding only if two or more spaces recorded it before the claim. <roam uid="sZ85qtOYg"/>
      - Stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs. <roam uid="SK6ZmyFfB"/>
      - Burden: none, but people in a single graph never reach this level. Cost: low, a query over existing rows. <roam uid="-I0HJIpta"/>
    - L3: Conflict detection and notification. Freeze a uid when a competing claim arrives; mail the verified address when a link is made. <roam uid="IjOxjCi1x"/>
      - Prevents nothing, but a forgery is noticed fast and can be reversed. <roam uid="QBboyIbUv"/>
      - Burden: the victim reacts to a notice; someone settles frozen links. Cost: low to medium. Platforms: all. <roam uid="R0WJRywXw"/>
      - Variant: the victim's plugin checks on load <roam uid="_lAmRuC9k"/>
        - The plugin knows the current Roam uid from its own client. On load it asks whether that `PlatformAccount` is claimed. If it is claimed and the person has no personal session, or a different one, the plugin asks "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" <roam uid="FNfpjab1n"/>
        - Catches a forgery without email, even when the forger controls the email binding. The damage window lasts until the victim next opens the plugin. <roam uid="ovhYlp3bV"/>
        - Needs a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function that returns only the claim status, not the claimant. `my_accounts` no longer exposes `dg_account`. <roam uid="HU4VT8div"/>
        - Under the space session the caller only asserts their uid, so any member can ask about any co-member ("has X connected a Discourse Graphs account?"). With L8, the plugin can present the Firebase token and the function answers only for the proven uid. <roam uid="NxNh0_jLj"/>
        - Responding can't rest on a bare assertion: if anyone could freeze a claim, a forger could freeze every legitimate claim in the graph. A contest must either bring a proof stronger than the existing claim's attestation (L1, L8), or only notify and flag for review. <roam uid="03ZvE1H1-"/>
    - L4: Per-device keys, trusted on first use. The plugin silently registers a key per browser and Roam user; identity claims must be signed by a registered key. <roam uid="OlDRHI2bI"/>
      - Stops forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run. A key added later for the same uid shows up on the older device as "a new device was registered as you". <roam uid="oZz6BVWjI"/>
      - Burden: users confirm new devices. Cost: medium. Platforms: Roam and Obsidian. <roam uid="_Dcxp_ILa"/>
      - Works without a personal account, so it protects people who never sign up. <roam uid="qKkvxmlvM"/>
      - Caveat: in Roam, every extension shares the roamresearch.com origin. Another extension can use the key while the page is open, but can't export it. <roam uid="HNbfUd67I"/>
    - L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xp07QYFwB"/>
      - Stops forgery by anyone except the admin. <roam uid="H5d_3BrMU"/>
      - Burden: admins, once per claim. Cost: medium, needs the admin role first. Only as strong as the admin proof. <roam uid="hlhlB4Hzw"/>
    - L6: Roam backend attestation. Our server reads the uid-to-email binding from Roam with a graph token. <roam uid="xZ9ZW0mBc"/>
      - Stops all forgery. <roam uid="XbTu0uESn"/>
      - Needs an active Roam subscription to create a backend token. L6 can therefore only be an optional upgrade, never a requirement. <roam uid="aUGQqVVU0"/>
      - A Roam uid is global, so a one-time token from any graph the person owns is enough. No shared-graph admin is needed. <roam uid="-ubL7d6ZM"/>
      - Burden: the person supplies a token once (or an admin stores one). Cost: medium one-time, high if stored (secrets, rotation). Platforms: Roam only. <roam uid="csHZObWSP"/>
      - Variant: a token stored per graph, supplied by an admin. <roam uid="j0wLV46uO"/>
        - Our server can then attest the uid-to-email binding of any member of that graph. Members don't need their own Roam subscription, so L6 becomes available to everyone in that graph. <roam uid="xyNjRWm5g"/>
        - The same token can first attest the admin who supplies it, so their proven admin flag lands on the right `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="IskrgBXJ4"/>
        - Cost: a read-only graph token exposes the whole graph, which is far more than Discourse Graphs stores. It needs encrypted storage readable only by a server-side function (for example Supabase Vault), never by clients. The admin can revoke it in Roam at any time, and then the graph falls back to the weaker layers. <roam uid="WxoAJVdJR"/>
    - L7: Tiered space password. Members get a reader credential; admins hold the editor credential. <roam uid="ipLQprIac"/>
      - Stops forgery by non-admins. <roam uid="TD5X_nVgo"/>
      - Burden: admins distribute and rotate credentials. Cost: medium, and it changes who can sync. <roam uid="dE_FI2cS_"/>
    - L8: Roam sign-in token (candidate). The plugin reads the signed-in user's Firebase ID token from the page and sends it to our server, which checks it and discards it. <roam uid="J0BDirkni"/>
      - Roam uses Firebase Auth. Its ID token is a JWT signed by Google, with issuer `https://securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`. Its claims include the Roam uid (`sub`), the user's email, and `email_verified` (true in the test). The token expires after about an hour. Checked in the Roam desktop app on 2026-10-24. <roam uid="6BQcIhrfL"/>
      - Our server can check the signature against Google's public keys and the audience `firescript-577a2`, without any Roam token. A co-member can't produce another user's token without running code in that user's browser. <roam uid="V1kVD6tTP"/>
      - Stops all forgery, like L6, and works for every Roam user, with no subscription and no admin. <roam uid="zLeqJYcuA"/>
      - Burden: none for the person. Cost: low to medium, one server-side check. <roam uid="QJauyMm3T"/>
      - Caveats <roam uid="Mg5o9FT2O"/>
        - **Blocking: L8 can't be used until we have checked that it doesn't violate Roam's Terms of Service, and Roam has agreed.** Reading another product's session token and sending it to our server may breach those terms even if we only verify it and discard it. <roam uid="on38t4VGv"/>
        - It depends on Roam's internals: the token sits in IndexedDB (`firebaseLocalStorageDb`), which Roam can change without notice. <roam uid="e0BzqzHvE"/>
        - The token also authenticates to Roam itself for about an hour. Our server would briefly hold a credential that can act as the user in Roam. <roam uid="k0stwVkUB"/>
        - Only the short-lived ID token may leave the browser, never the refresh token. <roam uid="Q_jKLTAGF"/>
      - Also checked in a browser on 2026-10-24, in a normal and a private window: the same storage holds the same kind of token. The browser has one auth entry where the desktop app has two (the app adds a `-tx-writer` entry), so the plugin should read the `[DEFAULT]` entry. <roam uid="tRm3RsaGT"/>
  - Packages to compare <roam uid="N3CzNT6ji"/>
    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>
    - Medium: Minimal + L2 + L4. Co-member forgery is prevented, except before the victim's first plugin use. Burden: new-device prompts. <roam uid="lpEuCPPEP"/>
    - Strong: Medium + L6 with a one-time token, for people who have a Roam subscription. Forgery is prevented for them. Burden: one token per person, once. Everyone else stays at Medium. <roam uid="ES2_RxYVo"/>
    - Admin-centric: L0 + L5 + L3. Set aside with L5. <roam uid="zo5JtOuJ8"/>
    - Because L6 is optional, Medium is the strongest level every user can reach. In it, L4 does most of the work against co-member forgery. <roam uid="GELnQvnLI"/>
    - Strong for everyone, if L8 is allowed: Medium + L8. Forgery is prevented for every Roam user, with no token and no subscription. Depends on Roam's agreement and on its internals staying stable. <roam uid="tsWkLqVnK"/>
  - Applies to every option <roam uid="inXsU_Qm3"/>
    - Record an attestation level on each link (`asserted`, `corroborated`, `attested`) and let policies read the level, never the platform. This lets us start low and add layers without migrating policies. <roam uid="UfKqf9ASZ"/>
    - Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links. <roam uid="w7SPEavvQ"/>
    - Platform-specific verification is expected. Multi-user platforms (Roam) have a server that can attest identity; local single-user platforms (Obsidian) have no co-member to forge against. <roam uid="mk9A0_wN6"/>
    - Obsidian links stay `asserted` in every option. Obsidian attribution comes from the person's verified identifiers, not from the platform account. <roam uid="eGU1Y7Vyj"/>
- Decision: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this sets which spaces a personal account can read and act for. The open question, how far a weakly proven claim reaches, decides whether cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="NQeAiZ8V4"/>
  - Ruled out <roam uid="1FYnwOB2T"/>
    - A: copy `SpaceAccess` and group rows to the person. The copies outlive the relation they came from. <roam uid="BGRs-LBmc"/>
    - Any edge from a person to a space that skips the `PlatformAccount`. This rules out B (the person as a member of the space pseudo-user in `group_membership`) and a separate person-to-space table. <roam uid="FKZQENpx6"/>
      - The `PlatformAccount` is where a person exists inside a space. Authorship, `LocalAccess` and identifiers hang off it. <roam uid="Z4r63tySQ"/>
      - A second track could disagree with it: a person could have a space's access through one edge while their `PlatformAccount` in that space is unclaimed, or claimed by someone else. <roam uid="2xyckcERL"/>
  - Model: claims through a PlatformAccount <roam uid="j2yrxCKys"/>
    - A claim links a personal account to a `PlatformAccount`. The person then acts for spaces where that `PlatformAccount` has a `LocalAccess` row. <roam uid="GMJo8AmA_"/>
    - `my_user_accounts()` adds those spaces' pseudo-users and the spaces' groups. The depth is fixed: one extra join, no recursion. <roam uid="5xZCf-gL6"/>
    - A person can also be a direct member of real groups, for example as a group admin. <roam uid="BobollM8N"/>
  - Open: how far a claim reaches <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm"/>
    - Option 1: reach follows identity. <roam uid="tYOGxPCv6"/>
      - Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="KS_8ViwDE"/>
      - Access needs identity proof first, so cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision. <roam uid="K210qCY9T"/>
    - Option 2: reach scoped by attestation. Preferred so far. <roam uid="bpN-mO9lF"/>
      - The claim record holds the person, the `PlatformAccount`, the vouching space (the space whose session made the claim), and the attestation level. <roam uid="2GK3rGpKk"/>
      - An `asserted` claim gives access only in the vouching space. <roam uid="28rjLezNq"/>
      - A `corroborated` or `attested` claim gives access in every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="qmd_UoR4o"/>
      - A forged assertion stays in a space whose password the forger already holds, so it gains nothing. <roam uid="mSMyEGsZg"/>
      - Proving identity later widens the reach in place, with no new kind of record. <roam uid="yb6-e7E5i"/>
      - Cost: with weakly proven claims, the person connects each space once. <roam uid="YiPQJDhje"/>
      - Cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="9M61pEmt1"/>
  - Properties of the model <roam uid="6mRqlz_K_"/>
    - Lease: a last-seen time on `LocalAccess`. The plugin's space session already writes `LocalAccess` when the person is active, so renewing needs no personal session. <roam uid="ifJ1jpWX7"/>
    - Revocation: delete the `LocalAccess` row, let the lease expire, or remove the claim. <roam uid="b30OPBdFw"/>
    - Caps, for example read-only access through a space: a cap column on the claim. Permission functions must apply it, because `my_user_accounts()` returns bare ids. The agent access design notes the same cost. <roam uid="T1dfPIW2r"/>
    - Space admin: the group admin flag doesn't apply. The leaning is an admin flag and its strength on `LocalAccess`; see "Space admin" under the other open decisions. <roam uid="gKWGQT9Pb"/>
    - Visibility: claims stay private to the person. Space readers already see the space's `PlatformAccount` rows through `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="LzUYZ2I5u"/>
    - Sharing a space with a group: the rule "`SpaceAccess(G, S)` exists only while S's pseudo-user is a member of G" is checked on S, so an insert check enforces it unchanged. A person shares on behalf of the space. <roam uid="3zLQCYhH4"/>
    - Agent grants: the same pattern inside `my_user_accounts()` as `agent_grant`, but a different table. An agent has exactly one principal and is gated by its role claim. An agent owned by a person adds one level: agent, person, space, group. <roam uid="nc_m8SiQY"/>
  - Prerequisite <roam uid="huOP3R6up"/>
    - The `group_membership` insert hole is closed first (see Constraints). It lets any caller join a uid that has no members, and space pseudo-users have none, so it already exposes spaces today (found by reading the policy, not tested). <roam uid="EogAwWnXT"/>
- Access resolution (sketch) <roam uid="B1gZUizm5"/>
  - **Why it matters:** every access policy calls these functions, so they set what each caller reaches and add to the cost of every query. Most of this section is agreed; only the lease length is open. <roam uid="mcAP4xcAU"/>
  - Where the claim lives, without a new table <roam uid="Cq8Z7k1_K"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account`: the person who claimed the account (exists today). <roam uid="HI27RxILB"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.claim_attestation`: asserted, corroborated, attested, or frozen. <roam uid="LpZMlh92m"/>
    - `LocalAccess.vouched`: this space's session made the claim. <roam uid="Aw4Af4gJG"/>
    - `LocalAccess.last_seen`: the lease. <roam uid="vZYlXEL7h"/>
    - `LocalAccess` admin level and delegated flag: the space-admin decision. <roam uid="p3wczF1ke"/>
    - Each space's pseudo-user uid is needed. Today it is found through the anonymous `PlatformAccount`, whose `account_local_id` is `get_space_anonymous_email(platform, id)`. A `Space.principal_uid` column would be clearer. <roam uid="IRNBzF_Oa"/>
  - Three nested sets of uids for a caller <roam uid="mEKDhdnT_"/>
    - `self_to_spaces()`: the caller, plus the spaces the caller acts for through claims (reach rule, lease, not frozen). <roam uid="9DQlyb6HQ"/>
    - `self_to_groups()`: that, plus the groups of every uid in it. One pass over `group_membership`, no recursion. <roam uid="xgb-TmzcC"/>
    - `self_to_everyone()`: that, plus the `everyone` pseudo-user. Replaces `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="p_XEWf7L1"/>
    - These replace `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. Outside SQL, both names only appear in the generated `dbTypes.ts`. <roam uid="25IooWjth"/>
  - Which set each check uses <roam uid="bZ325OCEt"/>
    - Membership and admin checks on a group use `self_to_spaces()`. Groups don't count, otherwise membership would nest. `everyone` never counts. <roam uid="V3mJeIE0I"/>
    - Checks for sharing a space with an account use `self_to_groups()`. A public grant must not count as sharing. <roam uid="_xnlnN4_m"/>
    - Reads use `self_to_everyone()`. <roam uid="XOZ7nL4S6"/>
  - Each set is computed for one principal and works for any caller <roam uid="-7GZXBiOr"/>
    - Space session: the space and its groups, the same as today. <roam uid="INz7A6X98"/>
    - Person: the person, their direct groups, their claimed spaces, and those spaces' groups. <roam uid="9wwDV7p4T"/>
    - Agent: its own expansion, plus the full expansion of its principal from `agent_grant`. <roam uid="pul5mAdGy"/>
  - Group admin <roam uid="GNGlWJVoz"/>
    - Stage 1: `is_group_admin(G)` is true when any uid in `self_to_spaces()` is an admin of G. A person who acts for space S is an admin of G whenever S is. This lets people be promoted to direct group admins without being direct members first. <roam uid="gparhcgzS"/>
    - Stage 2: restrict the space-derived part to people who are admins of S. It waits until space admins exist. <roam uid="ziRKyT9d4"/>
    - The same rule applies to leaving a group: the `group_membership` delete policy would let a person make S leave G. Stage 2 restricts it too. <roam uid="FA4vWPAT2"/>
    - `my_pseudo_accounts` must check `self_to_spaces()` instead of `auth.uid()`. Otherwise a person never sees the groups of their spaces, and publishing to groups finds none. <roam uid="F5fgLmqoL"/>
  - Agreed <roam uid="cCtIzCldr"/>
    - Caps: the sets return each uid with a cap, as `TABLE(uid, cap)` rather than bare uids. Permission checks use the lower of the grant and the cap. A group reached through a capped space inherits the cap. The same mechanism covers read-only access through a space and read-only agents. <roam uid="vLHTviSzs"/>
    - Cost: for a person, each call walks `PlatformAccount`, `LocalAccess`, `Space` and `group_membership`. That is fine once per statement but not once per row, so the RLS rewrite to the `= ANY((SELECT ...))` pattern becomes a prerequisite. <roam uid="SyoGpN9DQ"/>
  - Open: the lease length (90 days is a placeholder). <roam uid="IN5YpaEA5"/>
- Other open decisions (not yet mapped in detail) <roam uid="W8f_RJZgt"/>
  - Space admin <roam uid="3l40D2TI3"/>

The weaker the admin proof, the easier it is for a co-member to take those powers, so the proof and the list of powers have to be decided together. <roam uid="YyVfTf1I1"/>
    - Guessed: the plugin reports who is admin. <roam uid="RBdmXSvZj"/>

It is synchronous, takes no parameters, and answers only for the current user. This replaces the earlier guess, the first user page created in the graph. <roam uid="SdqDeXOxt"/>
        - The plugin can't ask about other users, so an admin is recorded only once that admin runs the plugin. Until then the space has no admin at this tier. <roam uid="xP-d6GZl_"/>

      - Obsidian: the only user. <roam uid="L_SdOpU7g"/>
      - Website: the creator of the space. <roam uid="Gbpn8W21T"/>
      - Forgeable on every platform: the plugin sends the report under the space session, so a co-member who holds the space password can report themselves as admin. L8 would prove which Roam user is calling, but not that this user is an admin. In Roam, L6 closes the gap for the admin who supplies a backend token: only admins can create one, and the same token lets our server attest which Roam user they are. That admin moves to the proven tier; other admins stay guessed. <roam uid="yhMBFbag9"/>
    - Registered: the person who first connected the space. Not recorded today. <roam uid="BLTnvtton"/>
    - Proven: whoever supplies a working Roam backend token. Only graph owners and admins can create one. Tokens need an active Roam subscription, so this tier can only override a guess, never be the only way to become admin. <roam uid="9qNvUNN9F"/>
      - Proof without storage: the admin supplies a token, the server checks that it works for this graph, and discards it. <roam uid="mUOuMCo17"/>
      - Proof with storage: the admin agrees to keep the token, which also enables L6 for every member of the graph (see the stored-token variant under L6). <roam uid="2REL1pTdm"/>
      - The token shows that the submitter is an admin. It doesn't say which Roam user they are. The flag should only land on a `PlatformAccount` whose claim is stronger than `asserted`, or the same token should attest the submitter first. <roam uid="U_5nSbh0a"/>
    - How strong the proof must be depends on the list of admin-only powers, which is not defined yet. <roam uid="1Ay60cIYE"/>
    - Leaning: store the admin flag and its strength (guessed, registered, proven) on `LocalAccess`, so a `PlatformAccount` is admin in a space and a person inherits it through their claim. <roam uid="w0bP5wnBY"/>
      - Fits the guessed tier: "the first user page in the graph" names a Roam uid, which is a `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="6kIjZzHap"/>
      - Several admins per space come for free. Removing the `LocalAccess` row, or letting its lease expire, also removes the admin role. <roam uid="KhfJkTyoB"/>
      - Escalation risk with reach option 2: an `asserted` claim reaches the vouching space. If it also inherits the admin flag of the claimed account, a co-member can assert the admin's uid and become admin. Admin powers should therefore require both an admin flag on `LocalAccess` and a claim stronger than `asserted`. <roam uid="SEhF6UP4l"/>
      - Write protection: today space editors can write `LocalAccess` rows of unclaimed accounts, and owners can write their own. Neither may set the admin flag or its strength. Only a `SECURITY DEFINER` function (or column-level privileges) may write those columns. <roam uid="Ftrn9F8gW"/>
      - A stronger tier doesn't replace weaker admins automatically. An admin interface lets a proven admin demote guessed admins if they choose to. <roam uid="XTmTih6kQ"/>
        - This makes "demote an admin of a weaker tier" the first item on the list of admin-only powers. <roam uid="gSWDdOn6-"/>
        - Open: can an admin demote another admin of the same tier? A rule of "only strictly weaker tiers" stops two guessed admins from removing each other, but leaves no way out of a dispute between them except a stronger proof. <roam uid="x0aFCIehm"/>
    - Admin-only powers <roam uid="gE3hYX534"/>
      - How strong the admin proof must be depends on what admins can do beyond an editor. Today every graph member holds the space password, which acts as editor. <roam uid="fbg0cLP5y"/>
      - Agreed <roam uid="KT6If9giX"/>
        - Demote an admin of a weaker tier. <roam uid="r_FK4G0HP"/>
        - Supply a Roam backend token as proof, and choose whether we keep it. Keeping it is an explicit opt-in. <roam uid="9rNRYMpLf"/>
      - Leaning yes <roam uid="cFJHvwfPG"/>
        - Delete the token we stored, so it no longer exists on our side. (Revoking it in Roam is already up to the admin.) <roam uid="cgzSu3r0V"/>
        - Rotate the space password. Today nothing rotates it, and every past member keeps it. <roam uid="pFQ6fmnbM"/>
        - Join and leave groups on behalf of the space. Today any holder of the space password can accept a group invitation as the space. <roam uid="kx6217H3V"/>
        - Remove a person's access to the space by deleting their `LocalAccess` row, without waiting for the lease to expire. <roam uid="m6ei3fcOi"/>
      - Not an admin power <roam uid="ppu5VG1Sc"/>
        - Approving identity claims (layer L5). Set aside: it feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xoR7fN0tT"/>
        - Setting a policy for cross-space search. The leaning is to always allow it with read access (see "Consent for cross-space search"). <roam uid="T6NbhkV-b"/>
      - Delegate admins (leaning) <roam uid="yt9ViDH2K"/>
        - An admin can name delegate admins, who can use the admin powers even though the platform doesn't see them as admins. <roam uid="JoZfvsjTF"/>
        - Fits `LocalAccess`: a delegate is an admin flag whose level sits just below the delegating admin's level and above the next level down. Who delegated is not recorded. <roam uid="ndH91oosF"/>
          - Resulting order, weakest first: guessed-delegated, guessed, registered-delegated, registered, proven-delegated, proven. <roam uid="hjfsHe13t"/>
          - Two ways to store it: a six-value level, or the three tiers plus a `delegated` flag, compared on the tier first and then with delegated below non-delegated. They give the same order. <roam uid="PXUtvwxz6"/>
          - With the demotion rule (only strictly lower levels), a delegate of a proven admin can demote registered and guessed admins, but not the proven admin who named them. <roam uid="HJXkL5XUj"/>
        - A delegate can name further delegates, at the delegate's own level. Delegates at the same level can't demote each other. This keeps the system simple, which suits small teams. <roam uid="IPvSBnYxB"/>
        - A delegation doesn't end on its own when the admin who made it is demoted or leaves. Whoever demotes an admin also decides about the remaining delegates. <roam uid="S2wcRkuYG"/>
      - Each candidate moved to admins takes a power away from "anyone with the space password". Each one also raises the bar for the admin proof. <roam uid="TPTTRkHSH"/>
  - Personal session in the plugins <roam uid="v-wdJK626"/>
    - **Why it matters:** this sets how a person logs in from a plugin, and where the plugin keeps that login. In Roam, keeping the login across reloads exposes it to every other extension, and not keeping it costs a click after each reload. It also decides which work runs as the person and which as the space, because some functions break if the person replaces the space. <roam uid="XtAl_AlUO"/>
    - Delivery: leaning towards Supabase Auth acting as an OAuth server, with the plugin as an OAuth client (PKCE). The person logs in on the Website by whatever method their account uses, so password accounts work too. Fallback: a device-style flow over `secret_token`, where the plugin opens the Website and then polls for the session. <roam uid="anOlv9O2J"/>
      - The Supabase OAuth 2.1 Server has no separate charge. People who sign in through it count toward the project's monthly active users, like any other sign-in. Source: Supabase docs, OAuth 2.1 Server guide. Accepted as an added cost. <roam uid="Z6B0tGor7"/>
      - Completing the flow inside the plugin is nice to have, not required. If it can't, the flow completes in a browser tab: the Website receives the result and the plugin collects it through the `secret_token` fallback. <roam uid="HmGIe3SsJ"/>
      - Social login (Supabase `signInWithOAuth` and identity linking) is a separate need on the Website: adding external identities to an account, and logging in with them. <roam uid="THBV37Ayp"/>
      - A person may create their account with an external identity and keep logging in with it, without ever setting a password. The plugin flow works the same for them, because the login step happens on the Website. <roam uid="IrbMTsSJY"/>
      - External identities linked this way are verified by their provider, so they can also serve as trusted identifiers for attribution. ORCID is not a built-in provider (ENG-405). <roam uid="MtQhgD_oh"/>
    - Storage: never in graph settings or the vault's `data.json`, which other people can read or sync. In Roam, `localStorage` is shared with every extension. <roam uid="jQDFzycLX"/>
      - Supabase sets token lifetimes: the access token expires after the project's JWT expiry (one hour by default), and the refresh token lasts until it is used, revoked, or cut off by a session time-box or inactivity timeout, if the project sets one. <roam uid="sggTyBNKs"/>
      - These settings apply to the whole project, including Website sessions, not only to the plugins. <roam uid="qppZbZExq"/>
      - What the plugin decides is whether it keeps the refresh token: <roam uid="VNhkLUpxm"/>
        - Kept in `localStorage`: the session survives reloads, but any Roam extension can read the refresh token and act as the person. <roam uid="KiIUY_QsL"/>
        - Kept in memory only: the session ends at each page reload, and the plugin runs the OAuth flow again. <roam uid="6h1qgZaHl"/>
      - Re-running the flow is cheap: the Website keeps its own login cookie on its own origin, which Roam extensions can't read. If the person is still logged in on the Website, the flow completes without typing anything. <roam uid="Rnxg83ODf"/>
      - Roam never reads the Website's cookie. The plugin opens a popup on the Website, the popup uses the cookie to skip the login form, and the Website sends an authorization code back to the plugin's page. The plugin exchanges the code for its own tokens, separate from the Website's session. <roam uid="D7aP7KN83"/>
      - A popup needs a user click, so after a reload the person clicks once to reconnect. A hidden iframe could avoid the click, but browsers increasingly block the cookies it would need. <roam uid="z-uzA5aW1"/>
      - Memory-only storage stops theft of tokens at rest. It doesn't stop a malicious extension that is running in the same page while the session is active, for example by wrapping `fetch`. <roam uid="OAS1AAkJ6"/>
      - Pending: keep tokens in memory in Roam (one click to reconnect after each reload), or keep the refresh token in `localStorage` (no click, but other extensions can steal it). Obsidian can store tokens on disk outside the vault either way. <roam uid="5YETQsAFC"/>
    - Two sessions: the plugin keeps the space session and adds a personal session when one is available. <roam uid="A8N_Jsvr1"/>
      - Downsides of switching the plugin from the space session to the personal session when one is available <roam uid="esLlHtygy"/>
        - Reads are equivalent or wider: the person sees their space, plus every other space and group they reach. That is what cross-space search needs. <roam uid="ckoj72WSx"/>
        - Some functions use `auth.uid()` to mean "the space", so their behavior changes with a personal session: <roam uid="RwmJfxu2_"/>
          - `accept_group_invitation` adds `auth.uid()` to the group. With a personal session, the person joins the group instead of the space. That breaks the rule that a space is shared with a group only while the space's pseudo-user is a member. <roam uid="hpKF4x5Cr"/>
          - `my_pseudo_accounts` finds groups through `auth.uid()` being a member. A person who isn't a direct member sees no groups, so publishing to groups (`getPublishedGroupIdsByRid`) finds none. <roam uid="ZTcuCO_P6"/>
          - `upsert_account_in_space` writes a `SpaceAccess` row for any account whose `dg_account` is set. Once claims set `dg_account`, it would copy grants to the person, which option A ruled out. The branch has to go. <roam uid="0RzabN3lg"/>
        - Code that relies on RLS to keep results inside the current space would start returning other spaces' content. Plugin queries should filter by space explicitly. Not audited yet. <roam uid="g9oBrenl5"/>
        - The personal session can disappear in the middle of work: it is short-lived in Roam, its lease can expire, and a claim can be frozen by conflict detection. Sync must fall back to the space session without failing. <roam uid="c6U6CEgwk"/>
        - Each query pays for a larger `my_user_accounts()` set. This only matters for people in many spaces. <roam uid="4dMwUYBr6"/>
        - The space session can't be dropped: creating the space and acting as the space with groups still need it. <roam uid="-Mq1IUscM"/>
      - Split: the personal session for reads, search and actions done as the person; the space session for sync, group membership and sharing. <roam uid="OhtCf8HO2"/>
  - Consent for cross-space search <roam uid="fi-J8nr1F"/>
    - Today content crosses spaces only through a group both spaces joined. Search from the plugin lets a person bridge two spaces that never agreed. <roam uid="EUEJ5yT3O"/>
    - Options: a member's read access is enough, or each space sets a policy for being searched from other spaces. Leaning: read access is enough, with no space policy. <roam uid="cuMNT218A"/>
    - Cost of the leaning: a member of a private graph B can find B's content while working in graph A and import it into A. They could already copy it by hand, but the tool makes it routine, and B has no say. <roam uid="XhscC1bBd"/>
  - Personal information before consent (ENG-918) <roam uid="sPWWnb1Zg"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the plugins already store the names and emails of people who never agreed to it. This decides what other users can see of them, and how same-named people are told apart. <roam uid="ukHWWQ9Zr"/>
    - Plugins create `PlatformAccount` rows with names and emails before the person has agreed to anything. <roam uid="f_HUcUaFh"/>
    - Options: keep sending, hold names and emails until a link exists, or mask by default (as ENG-1837 does with `anonymous #<id>`). <roam uid="w5NITWyZl"/>
    - Leaning: expose names, and keep emails hidden until the person shares them explicitly. Emails are stored in any case. Same-named people are told apart by showing the name with the `PlatformAccount` id. <roam uid="xu0Zrp-lp"/>
      - This is about exposure, not storage. The plugins still send emails: identity layer L1 needs the stored email to check the uid-to-email binding. Only the person and server-side functions read it. <roam uid="b-WXuL0SL"/>
      - Cost: names aren't unique. Two people in a space can share a name, and imports across spaces can't tell same-named authors apart. <roam uid="5PDfzx8LK"/>
      - Ways to tell same-named people apart without emails: <roam uid="HrdY6jxk0"/>
        - Show the name with the `PlatformAccount` id, as ENG-1837 already does for `anonymous #<id>`. A Roam uid has one `PlatformAccount` in every graph, so the id also matches the same Roam user across spaces. Cheap, but not pretty. <roam uid="gZFaAP3K8"/>
        - Give claimed personal accounts a unique handle, chosen by the person. Unclaimed accounts keep the name and id. <roam uid="-pTyhBAKq"/>
        - An opaque id per person, computed on the server from the email with a secret salt. It is stable and unique, and doesn't reveal the email. Plain email hashes are not safe, because emails can be guessed. <roam uid="Rj_nty-bD"/>
      - Once an account is claimed, the profile name is shown, because it is the name most directly under the person's control. <roam uid="oXvuGtrd3"/>
  - Profile visibility <roam uid="S4MegNHAq"/>
    - Options: a visibility value per field, or access rows per field and audience in the style of `ResourceAccess`, with `everyone`, a group or shared-space peers as the audience. <roam uid="1HwtriyvB"/>
    - FEE-755 set the minimum profile to name and email, with ORCID later. <roam uid="2We7q8coS"/>
    - Leaning: one row per person and audience, in the style of `ResourceAccess`, holding an array of visible fields. <roam uid="lM4axaive"/>
      - The audience is a principal uid: `everyone`, a group, or a space pseudo-user. A space as audience means everyone who acts for that space, which fits the access model above. <roam uid="fYeVpSrjI"/>
      - A viewer usually belongs to several audiences, so the visible fields are the union of the arrays of every row whose audience is in the viewer's `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="NECKklm5j"/>
      - Compared with one row per field: fewer rows and one write per audience. The field names in the array need a check against the allowed set, since a foreign key can't do it. <roam uid="1jrgL3Jdh"/>
- Facts to verify before relying on them <roam uid="8okk-_Uer"/>
  - Answered: a Roam client can't set `:create/user` on its own writes. `roamAlphaAPI.data.block.create` ignores an attempt to set it to another user and records the caller, and the older `roamDatomicAlphaAPI` isn't present (tested from the console, 2026-10-24). A block's creator is therefore trustworthy evidence of which Roam user wrote it. <roam uid="I_T0KWw31" refs="1"/>
  - Does the Roam backend API return `:user/email` for users of the graph? <roam uid="pncmfqVMJ"/>
  - Does a Roam import keep the original `:create/user` and `:create/time`? <roam uid="ihRxT-Vwx"/>
  - ORCID: mostly answered. ORCID's own OAuth sign-in returns an authenticated ORCID iD, so the Website can verify an ORCID for attribution as its own OAuth client. Supabase also accepts custom OAuth and OIDC providers (identifier `custom:...`, up to 3 on the free plan, unlimited on Pro), so ORCID can be a login provider as well. Still open: whether linking a custom-provider identity to an existing account works (the docs don't say), and ORCID usually doesn't release an email, so the provider needs `email_optional`. <roam uid="4nPdcx1yb"/>
  - Answered: an Obsidian `PlatformAccount` is created by the plugin, with an id made of the vault name and a random suffix, stored in the plugin settings. It is local to one vault, but a vault synced between devices or people shares the same id. <roam uid="pcJRRqX-t"/>
  - Can the Supabase OAuth 2.1 Server flow complete inside the plugins? Roam has no protocol handler, so it would need a popup that hands the result back to the page. Obsidian can register an `obsidian://` handler. <roam uid="llUBOTvj7"/>
  - ATProto: its OAuth profile requires DPoP and pushed authorization requests, which a Supabase custom provider probably doesn't support (expected, not tested). Assume ATProto login or identity verification needs its own flow on the Website. The verified handle or `did:plc` would then be stored as a trusted identifier, like ORCID. <roam uid="E0XuKzFaB"/>
  - Can the Obsidian plugin read the email of the signed-in Obsidian account, and is that email verified? <roam uid="SnaEEHkZI"/>

# Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="8"/>

- [[>]] [[!NOTE]] Working document: options and their costs, not decisions <roam uid="S4dKzvDG9"/>
  - This page maps the options for adding personal accounts to Discourse Graphs, so the group can choose. Only the items under "Constraints so far" are settled. Part of [[Project/Discourse Graph Accounts]]. <roam uid="WOKj5fQ9w"/>
  - This was written with OpenSpec, but because there are many pending decisions, we decided to stay at a pre-spec level. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
- Constraints so far <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h"/>
  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone can join a uid that has no members yet) is closed before any of this work. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>
- Current state <roam uid="wV0qa8Lj7"/>
  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT"/>
    - One pseudo-user per space, with a shared space password stored in the platform settings. Every graph member can read that password. <roam uid="kb_Gd_svI"/>
    - One pseudo-user per group. <roam uid="IH0tyDi5Z"/>
    - The `everyone` pseudo-user for public content (ENG-1837 branch, not merged). <roam uid="oJCpZSrsO"/>
    - Agent users for read-only agent access (planned in the `agent-read-only-access` OpenSpec change). <roam uid="viJKLrjcB"/>
  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` already references `auth.users`. Today only the space pseudo-account sets it. <roam uid="f6tgGk3-t"/>
    - `upsert_account_in_space` already writes a `SpaceAccess` row for an account whose `dg_account` is set. This anticipates personal accounts with copied grants. <roam uid="umtrUcTmK"/>
  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK"/>
    - ENG-1837 adds `everyone` to it. The agent change adds the agent's principal and that principal's groups. Personal accounts would be the third change to this function. <roam uid="bUiWiBwvl"/>
  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`. An Obsidian account looks local to its vault (not verified). <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agent grants owned by a person: an agent reads what its person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
- Decision: how a personal account is linked to a platform identity <roam uid="HrW3SuczV"/>
  - **Why it matters:** anyone who holds a space password can claim to be any member of that space. This decision sets how much proof a link needs, and therefore whether a co-member can take over another member's attribution and their access to other spaces. Stronger proof costs the person effort or depends on Roam. <roam uid="G_ksAI6Q_"/>
  - The threat <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl"/>
    - Anyone with the space password can mint a claim as that space. In Roam, that is every graph member. <roam uid="3TQldEoEj"/>
    - A co-member can therefore claim another member's Roam uid and take over their attribution, and their access to other spaces if the claim spreads beyond the space. <roam uid="8miESmtZh"/>
    - Outsiders can't do this under any option below. <roam uid="EJZYtvlMR"/>
    - Example: Mallory reads graph A's space password, calls `create_secret_token` as the space with Alice's uid in the payload, opens the link, and logs in with her own Google account. `create_secret_token` accepts any payload from any authenticated caller. <roam uid="6gK3VqcE-"/>
  - Two kinds of claim <roam uid="_oWUtNrtr"/>
    - An access claim is an `asserted` claim: "I am this platform account", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have. <roam uid="qbzJP8qlz"/>
    - An identity claim says "this platform account is me". It carries attribution and may spread to other spaces, so it needs stronger proof. <roam uid="jriBBo825"/>
    - The group wants identity, not only access. <roam uid="tre8QheiL"/>
  - Verified identifiers are separate from links <roam uid="o_xM2FmbI"/>
    - A personal account can hold verified identifiers that aren't tied to any platform account: emails, Google or GitHub identities, an ORCID iD, an ATProto handle. <roam uid="rvWITqil4"/>
    - They serve login, the profile, and attribution on their own. <roam uid="cMWL7UAPb"/>
    - An identifier becomes evidence for a link only when a platform records the same identifier for a platform account. That is what L1 checks for email. <roam uid="Q1mfw83z-"/>
    - Obsidian attribution relies on these identifiers, since Obsidian rarely records anything we can check. <roam uid="dPJOYzQfI"/>
  - Email as the bridge <roam uid="WbpaSzu1V"/>
    - The Roam plugin can read `:user/email` through datalog. <roam uid="q37Xq8DVO"/>
    - If the personal account proves control of an email (Google login, or a verification mail) and Roam records that email for the uid, a forger fails: they can't log in as the victim's email. <roam uid="Zt5yx9RoU"/>
    - The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. If it comes from the claim's own payload, the forger writes their own email. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts. <roam uid="Qr1nAWi-I"/>
  - Layers <roam uid="tZGbhisXM"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the layers are the choices for the identity-link decision. Each one stops a different kind of forgery, at a different cost to the person and to us. The packages below combine them, so read those first if you only want the trade-offs. <roam uid="jY7-WynXq"/>
    - The layers stack. Each one is described by what it stops and what it costs. <roam uid="fBoQ0vuf5"/>
    - L0: Token handoff only. The plugin mints a `secret_token` with the uid; the person logs in on the Website. <roam uid="_qMYaUHJ0"/>
      - Stops outsiders only. <roam uid="ZjIn7a1og"/>
      - Burden: none. Cost: lowest, reuses the `auth/token` route. Platforms: all. <roam uid="bM5E9fXbZ"/>
    - L1: Email binding. The personal account must control the email that the platform records for the platform account. <roam uid="ShFzQ-cQE"/>
      - Control of the email can be proven two ways, both at this layer: a verification mail, or a linked external identity (Google, GitHub, ...) whose provider vouches that the email is verified. Many Roam users sign in to Roam with Google, so the same Google account often proves the match in one step. <roam uid="0ngOboLPC"/>
      - Only provider emails marked as verified count. Supabase also links identities that share a verified email automatically, so the account's set of verified emails must be read from the account, not from one login. <roam uid="L3hwsR2X1"/>
      - Stops a forger who can't also falsify the binding source. <roam uid="eNir7ER3F"/>
      - Burden: the person verifies once. Cost: low. The verification can start from any plugin or from the Website. Platforms: any platform that records an email for the account. Roam does; for Obsidian, see below. <roam uid="KgXX_YwXm"/>
      - Obsidian <roam uid="cx9aeX2_F"/>
        - The Obsidian plugin sends no email today (`email: undefined` in `supabaseContext.ts`). Whether it can read the email of the Obsidian account, and whether that email is verified, is not checked yet. Using an Obsidian account is optional, so some users have none. <roam uid="sx3sITsvn"/>
        - The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there. <roam uid="AM08ShSzs"/>
        - An email the person types in is not a platform record. Verifying it gives the personal account a verified identifier, but says nothing about which platform account is theirs. <roam uid="nvfy6pgBo"/>
        - A vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim by one of them covers the others' content too. <roam uid="vBcLpeOcv"/>
    - L2: Corroboration. Accept the binding only if two or more spaces recorded it before the claim. <roam uid="sZ85qtOYg"/>
      - Stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs. <roam uid="SK6ZmyFfB"/>
      - Burden: none, but people in a single graph never reach this level. Cost: low, a query over existing rows. <roam uid="-I0HJIpta"/>
    - L3: Conflict detection and notification. Freeze a uid when a competing claim arrives; mail the verified address when a link is made. <roam uid="IjOxjCi1x"/>
      - Prevents nothing, but a forgery is noticed fast and can be reversed. <roam uid="QBboyIbUv"/>
      - Burden: the victim reacts to a notice; someone settles frozen links. Cost: low to medium. Platforms: all. <roam uid="R0WJRywXw"/>
      - Variant: the victim's plugin checks on load <roam uid="_lAmRuC9k"/>
        - The plugin knows the current Roam uid from its own client. On load it asks whether that `PlatformAccount` is claimed. If it is claimed and the person has no personal session, or a different one, the plugin asks "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" <roam uid="FNfpjab1n"/>
        - Catches a forgery without email, even when the forger controls the email binding. The damage window lasts until the victim next opens the plugin. <roam uid="ovhYlp3bV"/>
        - Needs a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function that returns only the claim status, not the claimant. `my_accounts` no longer exposes `dg_account`. <roam uid="HU4VT8div"/>
        - Under the space session the caller only asserts their uid, so any member can ask about any co-member ("has X connected a Discourse Graphs account?"). With L8, the plugin can present the Firebase token and the function answers only for the proven uid. <roam uid="NxNh0_jLj"/>
        - Responding can't rest on a bare assertion: if anyone could freeze a claim, a forger could freeze every legitimate claim in the graph. A contest must either bring a proof stronger than the existing claim's attestation (L1, L8), or only notify and flag for review. <roam uid="03ZvE1H1-"/>
    - L4: Per-device keys, trusted on first use. The plugin silently registers a key per browser and Roam user; identity claims must be signed by a registered key. <roam uid="OlDRHI2bI"/>
      - Stops forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run. A key added later for the same uid shows up on the older device as "a new device was registered as you". <roam uid="oZz6BVWjI"/>
      - Burden: users confirm new devices. Cost: medium. Platforms: Roam and Obsidian. <roam uid="_Dcxp_ILa"/>
      - Works without a personal account, so it protects people who never sign up. <roam uid="qKkvxmlvM"/>
      - Caveat: in Roam, every extension shares the roamresearch.com origin. Another extension can use the key while the page is open, but can't export it. <roam uid="HNbfUd67I"/>
    - L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xp07QYFwB"/>
      - Stops forgery by anyone except the admin. <roam uid="H5d_3BrMU"/>
      - Burden: admins, once per claim. Cost: medium, needs the admin role first. Only as strong as the admin proof. <roam uid="hlhlB4Hzw"/>
    - L6: Roam backend attestation. Our server reads the uid-to-email binding from Roam with a graph token. <roam uid="xZ9ZW0mBc"/>
      - Stops all forgery. <roam uid="XbTu0uESn"/>
      - Needs an active Roam subscription to create a backend token. L6 can therefore only be an optional upgrade, never a requirement. <roam uid="aUGQqVVU0"/>
      - A Roam uid is global, so a one-time token from any graph the person owns is enough. No shared-graph admin is needed. <roam uid="-ubL7d6ZM"/>
      - Burden: the person supplies a token once (or an admin stores one). Cost: medium one-time, high if stored (secrets, rotation). Platforms: Roam only. <roam uid="csHZObWSP"/>
      - Variant: a token stored per graph, supplied by an admin. <roam uid="j0wLV46uO"/>
        - Our server can then attest the uid-to-email binding of any member of that graph. Members don't need their own Roam subscription, so L6 becomes available to everyone in that graph. <roam uid="xyNjRWm5g"/>
        - The same token can first attest the admin who supplies it, so their proven admin flag lands on the right `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="IskrgBXJ4"/>
        - Cost: a read-only graph token exposes the whole graph, which is far more than Discourse Graphs stores. It needs encrypted storage readable only by a server-side function (for example Supabase Vault), never by clients. The admin can revoke it in Roam at any time, and then the graph falls back to the weaker layers. <roam uid="WxoAJVdJR"/>
    - L7: Tiered space password. Members get a reader credential; admins hold the editor credential. <roam uid="ipLQprIac"/>
      - Stops forgery by non-admins. <roam uid="TD5X_nVgo"/>
      - Burden: admins distribute and rotate credentials. Cost: medium, and it changes who can sync. <roam uid="dE_FI2cS_"/>
    - L8: Roam sign-in token (candidate). The plugin reads the signed-in user's Firebase ID token from the page and sends it to our server, which checks it and discards it. <roam uid="J0BDirkni"/>
      - Roam uses Firebase Auth. Its ID token is a JWT signed by Google, with issuer `https://securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`. Its claims include the Roam uid (`sub`), the user's email, and `email_verified` (true in the test). The token expires after about an hour. Checked in the Roam desktop app on 2026-10-24. <roam uid="6BQcIhrfL"/>
      - Our server can check the signature against Google's public keys and the audience `firescript-577a2`, without any Roam token. A co-member can't produce another user's token without running code in that user's browser. <roam uid="V1kVD6tTP"/>
      - Stops all forgery, like L6, and works for every Roam user, with no subscription and no admin. <roam uid="zLeqJYcuA"/>
      - Burden: none for the person. Cost: low to medium, one server-side check. <roam uid="QJauyMm3T"/>
      - Caveats <roam uid="Mg5o9FT2O"/>
        - **Blocking: L8 can't be used until we have checked that it doesn't violate Roam's Terms of Service, and Roam has agreed.** Reading another product's session token and sending it to our server may breach those terms even if we only verify it and discard it. <roam uid="on38t4VGv"/>
        - It depends on Roam's internals: the token sits in IndexedDB (`firebaseLocalStorageDb`), which Roam can change without notice. <roam uid="e0BzqzHvE"/>
        - The token also authenticates to Roam itself for about an hour. Our server would briefly hold a credential that can act as the user in Roam. <roam uid="k0stwVkUB"/>
        - Only the short-lived ID token may leave the browser, never the refresh token. <roam uid="Q_jKLTAGF"/>
      - Also checked in a browser on 2026-10-24, in a normal and a private window: the same storage holds the same kind of token. The browser has one auth entry where the desktop app has two (the app adds a `-tx-writer` entry), so the plugin should read the `[DEFAULT]` entry. <roam uid="tRm3RsaGT"/>
  - Packages to compare <roam uid="N3CzNT6ji"/>
    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>
    - Medium: Minimal + L2 + L4. Co-member forgery is prevented, except before the victim's first plugin use. Burden: new-device prompts. <roam uid="lpEuCPPEP"/>
    - Strong: Medium + L6 with a one-time token, for people who have a Roam subscription. Forgery is prevented for them. Burden: one token per person, once. Everyone else stays at Medium. <roam uid="ES2_RxYVo"/>
    - Admin-centric: L0 + L5 + L3. Set aside with L5. <roam uid="zo5JtOuJ8"/>
    - Because L6 is optional, Medium is the strongest level every user can reach. In it, L4 does most of the work against co-member forgery. <roam uid="GELnQvnLI"/>
    - Strong for everyone, if L8 is allowed: Medium + L8. Forgery is prevented for every Roam user, with no token and no subscription. Depends on Roam's agreement and on its internals staying stable. <roam uid="tsWkLqVnK"/>
  - Applies to every option <roam uid="inXsU_Qm3"/>
    - Record an attestation level on each link (`asserted`, `corroborated`, `attested`) and let policies read the level, never the platform. This lets us start low and add layers without migrating policies. <roam uid="UfKqf9ASZ"/>
    - Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links. <roam uid="w7SPEavvQ"/>
    - Platform-specific verification is expected. Multi-user platforms (Roam) have a server that can attest identity; local single-user platforms (Obsidian) have no co-member to forge against. <roam uid="mk9A0_wN6"/>
    - Obsidian links stay `asserted` in every option. Obsidian attribution comes from the person's verified identifiers, not from the platform account. <roam uid="eGU1Y7Vyj"/>
- Decision: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this sets which spaces a personal account can read and act for. The open question, how far a weakly proven claim reaches, decides whether cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="NQeAiZ8V4"/>
  - Ruled out <roam uid="1FYnwOB2T"/>
    - A: copy `SpaceAccess` and group rows to the person. The copies outlive the relation they came from. <roam uid="BGRs-LBmc"/>
    - Any edge from a person to a space that skips the `PlatformAccount`. This rules out B (the person as a member of the space pseudo-user in `group_membership`) and a separate person-to-space table. <roam uid="FKZQENpx6"/>
      - The `PlatformAccount` is where a person exists inside a space. Authorship, `LocalAccess` and identifiers hang off it. <roam uid="Z4r63tySQ"/>
      - A second track could disagree with it: a person could have a space's access through one edge while their `PlatformAccount` in that space is unclaimed, or claimed by someone else. <roam uid="2xyckcERL"/>
  - Model: claims through a PlatformAccount <roam uid="j2yrxCKys"/>
    - A claim links a personal account to a `PlatformAccount`. The person then acts for spaces where that `PlatformAccount` has a `LocalAccess` row. <roam uid="GMJo8AmA_"/>
    - `my_user_accounts()` adds those spaces' pseudo-users and the spaces' groups. The depth is fixed: one extra join, no recursion. <roam uid="5xZCf-gL6"/>
    - A person can also be a direct member of real groups, for example as a group admin. <roam uid="BobollM8N"/>
  - Open: how far a claim reaches <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm"/>
    - Option 1: reach follows identity. <roam uid="tYOGxPCv6"/>
      - Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="KS_8ViwDE"/>
      - Access needs identity proof first, so cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision. <roam uid="K210qCY9T"/>
    - Option 2: reach scoped by attestation. Preferred so far. <roam uid="bpN-mO9lF"/>
      - The claim record holds the person, the `PlatformAccount`, the vouching space (the space whose session made the claim), and the attestation level. <roam uid="2GK3rGpKk"/>
      - An `asserted` claim gives access only in the vouching space. <roam uid="28rjLezNq"/>
      - A `corroborated` or `attested` claim gives access in every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="qmd_UoR4o"/>
      - A forged assertion stays in a space whose password the forger already holds, so it gains nothing. <roam uid="mSMyEGsZg"/>
      - Proving identity later widens the reach in place, with no new kind of record. <roam uid="yb6-e7E5i"/>
      - Cost: with weakly proven claims, the person connects each space once. <roam uid="YiPQJDhje"/>
      - Cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="9M61pEmt1"/>
  - Properties of the model <roam uid="6mRqlz_K_"/>
    - Lease: a last-seen time on `LocalAccess`. The plugin's space session already writes `LocalAccess` when the person is active, so renewing needs no personal session. <roam uid="ifJ1jpWX7"/>
    - Revocation: delete the `LocalAccess` row, let the lease expire, or remove the claim. <roam uid="b30OPBdFw"/>
    - Caps, for example read-only access through a space: a cap column on the claim. Permission functions must apply it, because `my_user_accounts()` returns bare ids. The agent access design notes the same cost. <roam uid="T1dfPIW2r"/>
    - Space admin: the group admin flag doesn't apply. The leaning is an admin flag and its strength on `LocalAccess`; see "Space admin" under the other open decisions. <roam uid="gKWGQT9Pb"/>
    - Visibility: claims stay private to the person. Space readers already see the space's `PlatformAccount` rows through `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="LzUYZ2I5u"/>
    - Sharing a space with a group: the rule "`SpaceAccess(G, S)` exists only while S's pseudo-user is a member of G" is checked on S, so an insert check enforces it unchanged. A person shares on behalf of the space. <roam uid="3zLQCYhH4"/>
    - Agent grants: the same pattern inside `my_user_accounts()` as `agent_grant`, but a different table. An agent has exactly one principal and is gated by its role claim. An agent owned by a person adds one level: agent, person, space, group. <roam uid="nc_m8SiQY"/>
  - Prerequisite <roam uid="huOP3R6up"/>
    - The `group_membership` insert hole is closed first (see Constraints). It lets any caller join a uid that has no members, and space pseudo-users have none, so it already exposes spaces today (found by reading the policy, not tested). <roam uid="EogAwWnXT"/>
- Access resolution (sketch) <roam uid="B1gZUizm5"/>
  - **Why it matters:** every access policy calls these functions, so they set what each caller reaches and add to the cost of every query. Most of this section is agreed; only the lease length is open. <roam uid="mcAP4xcAU"/>
  - Where the claim lives, without a new table <roam uid="Cq8Z7k1_K"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account`: the person who claimed the account (exists today). <roam uid="HI27RxILB"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.claim_attestation`: asserted, corroborated, attested, or frozen. <roam uid="LpZMlh92m"/>
    - `LocalAccess.vouched`: this space's session made the claim. <roam uid="Aw4Af4gJG"/>
    - `LocalAccess.last_seen`: the lease. <roam uid="vZYlXEL7h"/>
    - `LocalAccess` admin level and delegated flag: the space-admin decision. <roam uid="p3wczF1ke"/>
    - Each space's pseudo-user uid is needed. Today it is found through the anonymous `PlatformAccount`, whose `account_local_id` is `get_space_anonymous_email(platform, id)`. A `Space.principal_uid` column would be clearer. <roam uid="IRNBzF_Oa"/>
  - Three nested sets of uids for a caller <roam uid="mEKDhdnT_"/>
    - `self_to_spaces()`: the caller, plus the spaces the caller acts for through claims (reach rule, lease, not frozen). <roam uid="9DQlyb6HQ"/>
    - `self_to_groups()`: that, plus the groups of every uid in it. One pass over `group_membership`, no recursion. <roam uid="xgb-TmzcC"/>
    - `self_to_everyone()`: that, plus the `everyone` pseudo-user. Replaces `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="p_XEWf7L1"/>
    - These replace `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. Outside SQL, both names only appear in the generated `dbTypes.ts`. <roam uid="25IooWjth"/>
  - Which set each check uses <roam uid="bZ325OCEt"/>
    - Membership and admin checks on a group use `self_to_spaces()`. Groups don't count, otherwise membership would nest. `everyone` never counts. <roam uid="V3mJeIE0I"/>
    - Checks for sharing a space with an account use `self_to_groups()`. A public grant must not count as sharing. <roam uid="_xnlnN4_m"/>
    - Reads use `self_to_everyone()`. <roam uid="XOZ7nL4S6"/>
  - Each set is computed for one principal and works for any caller <roam uid="-7GZXBiOr"/>
    - Space session: the space and its groups, the same as today. <roam uid="INz7A6X98"/>
    - Person: the person, their direct groups, their claimed spaces, and those spaces' groups. <roam uid="9wwDV7p4T"/>
    - Agent: its own expansion, plus the full expansion of its principal from `agent_grant`. <roam uid="pul5mAdGy"/>
  - Group admin <roam uid="GNGlWJVoz"/>
    - Stage 1: `is_group_admin(G)` is true when any uid in `self_to_spaces()` is an admin of G. A person who acts for space S is an admin of G whenever S is. This lets people be promoted to direct group admins without being direct members first. <roam uid="gparhcgzS"/>
    - Stage 2: restrict the space-derived part to people who are admins of S. It waits until space admins exist. <roam uid="ziRKyT9d4"/>
    - The same rule applies to leaving a group: the `group_membership` delete policy would let a person make S leave G. Stage 2 restricts it too. <roam uid="FA4vWPAT2"/>
    - `my_pseudo_accounts` must check `self_to_spaces()` instead of `auth.uid()`. Otherwise a person never sees the groups of their spaces, and publishing to groups finds none. <roam uid="F5fgLmqoL"/>
  - Agreed <roam uid="cCtIzCldr"/>
    - Caps: the sets return each uid with a cap, as `TABLE(uid, cap)` rather than bare uids. Permission checks use the lower of the grant and the cap. A group reached through a capped space inherits the cap. The same mechanism covers read-only access through a space and read-only agents. <roam uid="vLHTviSzs"/>
    - Cost: for a person, each call walks `PlatformAccount`, `LocalAccess`, `Space` and `group_membership`. That is fine once per statement but not once per row, so the RLS rewrite to the `= ANY((SELECT ...))` pattern becomes a prerequisite. <roam uid="SyoGpN9DQ"/>
  - Open: the lease length (90 days is a placeholder). <roam uid="IN5YpaEA5"/>
- Other open decisions (not yet mapped in detail) <roam uid="W8f_RJZgt"/>

The weaker the admin proof, the easier it is for a co-member to take those powers, so the proof and the list of powers have to be decided together. <roam uid="YyVfTf1I1"/>
    - Guessed: the plugin reports who is admin. <roam uid="RBdmXSvZj"/>
