{"id":"P-FEE-149","uuid":"2c231fe0-c865-47e1-8aea-bda2744d2002","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"Real-time collaboration on shared tldraw board (roam, single-graph)","summary":"","description":"### Overview

Enable **real-time collaboration** on a shared **tldraw canvas inside Roam**, using a **single-graph model** (no inter-graph sync). This work introduces a third-party real-time sync backend so multiple users can edit the same canvas concurrently with low latency and consistent state.

This project focuses on **productionizing tldraw’s** `tldraw_sync` template, deploying it via **Cloudflare**, and updating Roam’s tldraw integration so eligible graphs use the external sync server as the authoritative source.

**In scope**

* Single-graph real-time sync only
  * One Roam graph ↔ one shared tldraw room
  * No cross-graph or federated sync
* Use tldraw’s `tldraw_sync` reference implementation as the baseline
* Deploy and operate the sync server on Cloudflare
* Update Roam tldraw integration to:
  * Route eligible canvases through the sync server
  * Fall back to local/non-sync mode when disabled
* Define:
  * Who is allowed to use real-time sync
  * How access is granted and revoked
  * What data is stored on the sync server
  * Retention, cleanup, and failure behavior

**Out of scope**

* Inter-graph sync
* Cross-workspace collaboration
* Fine-grained permissions within a single canvas (initially)
* Offline-first guarantees beyond tldraw defaults","url":"https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/real-time-collaboration-on-shared-tldraw-board-roam-single-graph-6693532faedb","resourceCount":2,"createdAt":"2025-12-27T02:21:42.098Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-25T19:17:17.034Z","startedAt":"2026-01-06T19:40:54.731Z","completedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"startDate":"2026-01-06","startDateResolution":null,"targetDate":null,"targetDateResolution":null,"priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"labels":["Roam","New Feature"],"initiatives":[{"id":"4d3478ef-d78a-4522-83d1-b5ed658a9651","name":"Get Roam DG ready for moderate tolerance users"}],"lead":{"id":"9ef754d2-efb6-40b1-abbf-38a6b57aeeeb","name":"Michael Gartner"},"leadTeam":{"id":"3e71abb3-47b8-4432-885e-69edb696574a","name":"Feedback","key":"FEE"},"status":{"id":"f256c0ab-b05d-478f-a294-08d51daa954a","name":"In Progress","type":"started"},"teams":[{"id":"3e71abb3-47b8-4432-885e-69edb696574a","name":"Feedback","key":"FEE"},{"id":"5601a70b-bf83-4602-84c2-c45db7e1feff","name":"Product","key":"PRO"},{"id":"25bee64e-71aa-4c83-af3b-7fb4976f80b1","name":"Design","key":"DES"},{"id":"e69757b7-976a-4567-836f-16f8a4d59df2","name":"Engineering","key":"ENG"}]}

content.text:
{"id":"P-DIS-140","uuid":"a7b4bbc1-f729-4248-8b8b-b9bf01ab7ca7","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes","summary":"Upload a PDF to a web page and have AI extract nodes","description":"# <linear-comment id="11549f99-1c47-4faa-bcd8-0e7c97dc2afa" resolved="false">DG AI Paper Extraction — MVP-0 Scope</linear-comment>

> **Status:** Draft — Approved. 

---

1\. Goal + Non-Goals

### Goal

Standalone page on discoursegraphs.com: upload one PDF → get draft DG nodes with supporting snippets → review → select → copy to clipboard.

MVP-0 delivers one architecturally sound, mergeable, end-to-end flow. The point is not optimized extraction — it's a working flow that lets real users evaluate extraction quality, node taxonomy, and UX.

### Non-Goals

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| ✗ | Solving extraction quality in a final or optimized way. |
| ✗ | Automating publishing into Roam or Obsidian. |
| ✗ | Supporting all paper types, schemas, or edge cases. |
| ✗ | Building production-grade evaluation infrastructure. |
| ✗ | Batch processing or multi-paper upload. |
| ✗ | Relation extraction (nodes only, per [Jan 20 All Hands](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vDuO_Slg5>)). |

### Discourse Graph Context

This project is grounded in `[[FUN]]` - [Formulate research directions and experiments from conversation with / synthesis of literature](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Z1nI1LxMl>): *"The goal is to be able to annotate, capture, and reuse the key information stored in published papers."*

It targets the "taking and making notes" portion of that `FUN`. The closest existing manual precedent is `[[FLO]]` - [Make DG literature notes on a research source](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FFE29QvNt>) — Alpha status, weekly frequency, high impact. That flow involves reading a paper, pasting screenshots / writing notes, and using `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Roam)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/uILBlKlyz>) to create individual nodes manually.

**Adjacent context:**

* `[[FLO]]` - [Create citeable entry for a paper in Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/ioHOXjpaT>) — upstream prereq
* `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Obsidian)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/_Gn_XBvow>) — Obsidian-side analog (less developed)
* `[[FLO]]` - [Prepare and send nodes to page for synthesis](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FHEvBk5D7>) — downstream adjacent (different FUN, but where extracted nodes eventually go)
* `[[ISS]]` - [AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/lcuLhptzE>) — the issue that spawned this project
* `[[ART]]` - [Roam DG/Discourse Graph this Page](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/GvUUWUOua>) — prior art for auto-generating DG from content

**Proposed new nodes** (to be created as part of this work — not yet in graph):

* A new `FLO` for the AI-assisted extraction flow
* A new `ART` for the extraction feature on discoursegraphs.com

---

## 2. Architecture

This section defines the system design and domain boundaries for the extraction feature. MVP-0 implements a thin slice; the design should hold up as the project expands without prescribing what that expansion looks like.

### 2.1 Domain Model

| Concept | Description | MVP-0 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Paper** | An uploaded academic PDF. | Transient in MVP-0. |
| **Extraction Run** | One invocation of the pipeline against a paper with specific settings (node types, research question). | Ephemeral in MVP-0. |
| **Extracted Node** | A single extracted DG node: type tag, content, supporting snippet. | Rendered in the browser in MVP-0, copied as plain text. |
| **Evaluation** | A judgment about extraction quality on a known (paper, DG) pair. | Manual notes in Roam for MVP-0. |

### 2.2 System Layers

Three layers, each independently improvable:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Frontend Review App                                    │
│  Page on discoursegraphs.com. Handles upload,           │
│  configuration, result display, selection, and export.  │
│                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Extraction Engine: LLM                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Evaluation Layer                                       │
│  Compares extraction output against known graphs.       │
│  MVP-0: manual workflow, notes in Roam.                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The engine is the part that improves most over time. The interface between engine and frontend (the extracted node schema) should be stable even as internals change.

### 2.3 Key Design Decisions

* <linear-comment id="1fef4528-9b50-4fa6-8e0d-fb291064b1f5" resolved="true">**Extracted node schema**</linear-comment> **is the contract.** The extraction engine returns extracted-nodes in a normalized schema. The frontend consumes it. The evaluation layer compares against it. This is the seam that lets each layer evolve independently.
  * nodeType type definiton minimum:
    * label
    * definition
    * claimTag
* **The extraction engine is a pipeline, not a monolith.** pdf paper, prompt, model, and output formatter are separate concerns. MVP-0 wires them simply; any stage can be swapped later.
* **This lives inside the existing** `apps/website`. The Next.js app already has LLM API routes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), Supabase integration, Tailwind, and Vercel hosting. New routes and pages follow existing patterns.

### 2.4 Architectural Constraints

* Prompt, parser/chunker(llm now), model, and formatter must be swappable without changing the frontend.
* The evaluation workflow reuses the same extracted nodes output format as the frontend.
* No multi-pass, ensemble, RL, or retrieval-refinement in MVP-0.
* No direct write-back to Roam or Obsidian.

### 2.5 M0 Deliverable

Agree on:

1. The Extracted node schema (fields, types, what the frontend expects)
2. The extraction request/response contract (what the API route accepts and returns)
3. Confirmation that the layer boundaries above are right

---

## 3. V0 Scope

### Flow

```
Upload one PDF
  → Optionally enter a target research question
  → Review/toggle default node types before running
  → Run extraction
  → Review extracted nodes — each shows type tag + content + supporting snippet
  → Select desired blocks
  → Copy selected as plain text to clipboard
```

### In-Scope Use Cases

| ID | Description |
| -- | -- |
| UC1 | Upload a single academic paper PDF and get extracted DG nodes |
| UC2 | Optionally scope extraction to a target research question |
| UC3 | Toggle node types on/off from a default set before running |
| UC4 | Review each extracted node against its supporting snippet |
| UC5 | <linear-comment id="419d4fd7-9c92-4153-a75d-b91e57586cf3" resolved="false">Select and copy extracted node as plain text for use in </linear-comment> |
| UC6 | <linear-comment id="0990f58f-c5a2-4bd7-84ee-eafe914a4694" resolved="false">Joel and Matt manually compare extraction results against known benchmark datasets</linear-comment> (eval TBD) |

### Out of Scope

* Multiple papers / batch processing
* Custom user-defined node types
* Roam/Obsidian formatted export or direct object creation
* Image/table CDN hosting (LLM references fig/table numbers instead)
* Semantic Reader integration
* Advanced extraction (multi-pass, RL, ensemble, retrieval-augmented)
* Automated evaluation tooling or new eval-specific datastore
* Full auth or multi-user accounts

### Constraints / Assumptions

* One agreed end-to-end flow, not every possible branch.
* Default node-type set and tag labels are a **dependency on Matt/Joel**. Target types from the configured graph schema: CLM, EVD, QUE, RES, THE, Source. Exact subset to be confirmed before M1.
* Output is plain text; downstream formatting handled by user.
* Manual review is part of the product, not a fallback.
* Flow over polish; design can be simple and library-driven.
* Code must be production-worthy: clear boundaries, maintainable, mergeable to main.
* MVP-0 must only affect opted-in users and must not modify existing data.
* Security: LLM keys server-side on Vercel. Hard spending cap, spending alerts, easy key revocation. No shared user datastore. Worst case = token drain.
* Evaluation
  * Evaluation results will be recorded in Roam
    * user will copy and paste from the app and manually add feedback
    * can use <issue id="951383f9-b49b-4248-a7f2-e716849b2b33" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1604/extraction-run-on-benchmark-papers-quality-documented">ENG-1604</issue> 
    * can use [\[\[ISS\]\] - Initial paper benchmark results from \[\[Project/AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes\]\]](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SNeqhmSBF>)

---

## 4. Milestones

[M0: Architecture + Contracts](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-be0f7fd4-3db1-4680-8579-503ade3a900f>)

> **Deliverable:** Agreed extracted node schema, nodeType schema, PDF parser choice (LLM), and confirmation of layer boundaries. **Acceptance:** Interfaces reviewed; prompt/parser/model swappable without frontend redesign. **Dependencies:** None.

[M1: API route setup + Default Prompt](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e480b1cb-bd25-4e21-a0f8-c569806967a5>)

> **Deliverable:** API route + settings and returns normalized extracted nodes. **Acceptance:** Sample paper processed end-to-end; each extracted includes tag, content, and support reference; works on 2-3 benchmark papers; prompt includes few-shot examples. **Dependencies:** M0; node-type set from Matt/Joel; baseline prompt.

<linear-comment id="7b40b257-b525-434a-adb9-69b69a57c69b" resolved="false">[M2: Frontend App](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e8677cd6-0a74-4a87-a0c2-664b0a3d49a8>)</linear-comment>

> **Deliverable:** Page on discoursegraphs.com — upload, configure, run, review, select, copy. **Acceptance:** User completes full flow in browser; blocks render clearly; clipboard works. **Dependencies:** Stable M1 output schema.

[M3: Evaluation Baseline](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-171e0e29-3097-49b2-a508-aaa2a6785b18>)

> **Deliverable:** Manual evaluation — extraction run on benchmark papers, quality documented. **Acceptance:** Joel and Matt each evaluate 2-3 papers against known graphs; observations in Roam; obvious quality gaps identified. **Dependencies:** M1 stable; benchmark papers available.

### [M4: Smoke Test + Review + Merge ](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-8aca861c-37fa-4607-b2cd-93cd867b41cf>)

> **Deliverable:** Team review of full flow, decision log, merge to main. **Acceptance:** 10-min smoke test; axis-specific feedback on extraction quality, taxonomy, UX; merged and accessible. **Dependencies:** M2, M3.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

### P0 — Must have

FR0 - <issue id="9b44a383-68ca-463a-b097-764223f6072a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1601">ENG-1601</issue>

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| FR1 | <issue id="287e58ad-2246-4484-ac8d-5f28f603325a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1592">ENG-1592</issue> |
| FR2 | <issue id="171b2065-a196-4c0f-8487-26215b8a4921" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1593">ENG-1593</issue> |
| FR3 | <issue id="ea927329-04f6-4a02-9bcb-fd88031cd343" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1594">ENG-1594</issue> |
| FR4 | <issue id="e04c6495-d75c-42a8-af3d-d08959155e1d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1602/api-to-send-uploaded-pdf-to-chosen-llms-to-parse-from-fr1">ENG-1602</issue>, uses FR6 prompt |
| FR5 | ~~Chunk by section where boundaries are detectable (Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion)~~ using llm parser, will be included in FR6 prompt |
| FR6 | <issue id="089a3b0d-2d3e-42f8-b1a4-117b137fc3c6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1595">ENG-1595</issue> |
| FR7 | Each extracted node includes: node type tag, node content, supporting quote or figure/table reference |
| FR8 | <issue id="7829f53b-e3c4-4e62-81b9-668b52be05c8" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1596">ENG-1596</issue> |
| FR9 | <issue id="675ea294-3530-40e0-bfd4-aed017be1037" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1597">ENG-1597</issue> |
| FR10 | <issue id="d2fb1278-5075-424e-b13f-1e44cc23fe01" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1598">ENG-1598</issue> |

### 5.5  Non-Functional

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| NFR1 | <linear-comment id="592cad65-4129-4ab8-9a06-301ac26221f6" resolved="true">Support references include enough location info for quick re-finding in the paper</linear-comment> |
| NFR2 | <linear-comment id="26d54b85-b754-4d37-8d5c-ef96c94c610b" resolved="true">Reasonable defaults so a first-time user completes the flow without setup</linear-comment> |

---

## 6. Open Questions + Risks

### Open Questions

| \# | Question |
| -- | -- |
| 2 | <linear-comment id="ec7498b7-673d-485a-89d2-bc9671281e34" resolved="true">What does the clipboard output format look like? Should it match the graph's `[[CLM]] - {content}` format?</linear-comment> |
| 3 | Which few-shot examples should the prompt include, and from which papers? |
| 4 | What size or runtime limits on uploaded PDFs? |
| 5 | LLM model choice for extraction — cost vs. quality vs. context window? |
| 6 | Should the new `FLO` and `ART` discourse nodes be created before or after M0? |
| 7 | <linear-comment id="f6dd60e1-5543-463e-9194-713966bd8f0d" resolved="true">What fields belong in the extracted node schema to support future persistence without over-engineering MVP-0?</linear-comment> |

### Risks

| Risk | Impact |
| -- | -- |
| PDF extraction quality varies across publishers and scan quality | Weak input → weak extracted nodes |
| Figure/table-heavy papers may produce weak support references | Poor verifiability for certain paper types |
| Single broad prompt may over- or under-extract depending on paper structure | Inconsistent output quality |
| Public endpoint introduces token-abuse risk if spending limits are too loose | Cost blowout |
| If the review UI doesn't make verification easy, feedback quality will be poor even if extraction is reasonable | Team learning bottleneck |
| LLM PDF extraction might be a black box | Unable to inspect what text/content was actually extracted |
| LLM PDF extraction uses vision model | Which costs more |

---

{"id":"P-DIS-140","uuid":"a7b4bbc1-f729-4248-8b8b-b9bf01ab7ca7","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes","summary":"Upload a PDF to a web page and have AI extract nodes","description":"# <linear-comment id="11549f99-1c47-4faa-bcd8-0e7c97dc2afa" resolved="false">DG AI Paper Extraction — MVP-0 Scope</linear-comment>

> **Status:** Draft — Approved. 

---

1\. Goal + Non-Goals

### Goal

Standalone page on discoursegraphs.com: upload one PDF → get draft DG nodes with supporting snippets → review → select → copy to clipboard.

MVP-0 delivers one architecturally sound, mergeable, end-to-end flow. The point is not optimized extraction — it's a working flow that lets real users evaluate extraction quality, node taxonomy, and UX.

### Non-Goals

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| ✗ | Solving extraction quality in a final or optimized way. |
| ✗ | Automating publishing into Roam or Obsidian. |
| ✗ | Supporting all paper types, schemas, or edge cases. |
| ✗ | Building production-grade evaluation infrastructure. |
| ✗ | Batch processing or multi-paper upload. |
| ✗ | Relation extraction (nodes only, per [Jan 20 All Hands](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vDuO_Slg5>)). |

### Discourse Graph Context

This project is grounded in `[[FUN]]` - [Formulate research directions and experiments from conversation with / synthesis of literature](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Z1nI1LxMl>): *"The goal is to be able to annotate, capture, and reuse the key information stored in published papers."*

It targets the "taking and making notes" portion of that `FUN`. The closest existing manual precedent is `[[FLO]]` - [Make DG literature notes on a research source](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FFE29QvNt>) — Alpha status, weekly frequency, high impact. That flow involves reading a paper, pasting screenshots / writing notes, and using `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Roam)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/uILBlKlyz>) to create individual nodes manually.

**Adjacent context:**

* `[[FLO]]` - [Create citeable entry for a paper in Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/ioHOXjpaT>) — upstream prereq
* `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Obsidian)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/_Gn_XBvow>) — Obsidian-side analog (less developed)
* `[[FLO]]` - [Prepare and send nodes to page for synthesis](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FHEvBk5D7>) — downstream adjacent (different FUN, but where extracted nodes eventually go)
* `[[ISS]]` - [AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/lcuLhptzE>) — the issue that spawned this project
* `[[ART]]` - [Roam DG/Discourse Graph this Page](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/GvUUWUOua>) — prior art for auto-generating DG from content

**Proposed new nodes** (to be created as part of this work — not yet in graph):

* A new `FLO` for the AI-assisted extraction flow
* A new `ART` for the extraction feature on discoursegraphs.com

---

## 2. Architecture

This section defines the system design and domain boundaries for the extraction feature. MVP-0 implements a thin slice; the design should hold up as the project expands without prescribing what that expansion looks like.

### 2.1 Domain Model

| Concept | Description | MVP-0 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Paper** | An uploaded academic PDF. | Transient in MVP-0. |
| **Extraction Run** | One invocation of the pipeline against a paper with specific settings (node types, research question). | Ephemeral in MVP-0. |
| **Extracted Node** | A single extracted DG node: type tag, content, supporting snippet. | Rendered in the browser in MVP-0, copied as plain text. |
| **Evaluation** | A judgment about extraction quality on a known (paper, DG) pair. | Manual notes in Roam for MVP-0. |

### 2.2 System Layers

Three layers, each independently improvable:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Frontend Review App                                    │
│  Page on discoursegraphs.com. Handles upload,           │
│  configuration, result display, selection, and export.  │
│                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Extraction Engine: LLM                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Evaluation Layer                                       │
│  Compares extraction output against known graphs.       │
│  MVP-0: manual workflow, notes in Roam.                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The engine is the part that improves most over time. The interface between engine and frontend (the extracted node schema) should be stable even as internals change.

### 2.3 Key Design Decisions

* <linear-comment id="1fef4528-9b50-4fa6-8e0d-fb291064b1f5" resolved="true">**Extracted node schema**</linear-comment> **is the contract.** The extraction engine returns extracted-nodes in a normalized schema. The frontend consumes it. The evaluation layer compares against it. This is the seam that lets each layer evolve independently.
  * nodeType type definiton minimum:
    * label
    * definition
    * claimTag
* **The extraction engine is a pipeline, not a monolith.** pdf paper, prompt, model, and output formatter are separate concerns. MVP-0 wires them simply; any stage can be swapped later.
* **This lives inside the existing** `apps/website`. The Next.js app already has LLM API routes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), Supabase integration, Tailwind, and Vercel hosting. New routes and pages follow existing patterns.

### 2.4 Architectural Constraints

* Prompt, parser/chunker(llm now), model, and formatter must be swappable without changing the frontend.
* The evaluation workflow reuses the same extracted nodes output format as the frontend.
* No multi-pass, ensemble, RL, or retrieval-refinement in MVP-0.
* No direct write-back to Roam or Obsidian.

### 2.5 M0 Deliverable

Agree on:

1. The Extracted node schema (fields, types, what the frontend expects)
2. The extraction request/response contract (what the API route accepts and returns)
3. Confirmation that the layer boundaries above are right

---

## 3. V0 Scope

### Flow

```
Upload one PDF
  → Optionally enter a target research question
  → Review/toggle default node types before running
  → Run extraction
  → Review extracted nodes — each shows type tag + content + supporting snippet
  → Select desired blocks
  → Copy selected as plain text to clipboard
```

### In-Scope Use Cases

| ID | Description |
| -- | -- |
| UC1 | Upload a single academic paper PDF and get extracted DG nodes |
| UC2 | Optionally scope extraction to a target research question |
| UC3 | Toggle node types on/off from a default set before running |
| UC4 | Review each extracted node against its supporting snippet |
| UC5 | <linear-comment id="419d4fd7-9c92-4153-a75d-b91e57586cf3" resolved="false">Select and copy extracted node as plain text for use in </linear-comment> |
| UC6 | <linear-comment id="0990f58f-c5a2-4bd7-84ee-eafe914a4694" resolved="false">Joel and Matt manually compare extraction results against known benchmark datasets</linear-comment> (eval TBD) |

### Out of Scope

* Multiple papers / batch processing
* Custom user-defined node types
* Roam/Obsidian formatted export or direct object creation
* Image/table CDN hosting (LLM references fig/table numbers instead)
* Semantic Reader integration
* Advanced extraction (multi-pass, RL, ensemble, retrieval-augmented)
* Automated evaluation tooling or new eval-specific datastore
* Full auth or multi-user accounts

### Constraints / Assumptions

* One agreed end-to-end flow, not every possible branch.
* Default node-type set and tag labels are a **dependency on Matt/Joel**. Target types from the configured graph schema: CLM, EVD, QUE, RES, THE, Source. Exact subset to be confirmed before M1.
* Output is plain text; downstream formatting handled by user.
* Manual review is part of the product, not a fallback.
* Flow over polish; design can be simple and library-driven.
* Code must be production-worthy: clear boundaries, maintainable, mergeable to main.
* MVP-0 must only affect opted-in users and must not modify existing data.
* Security: LLM keys server-side on Vercel. Hard spending cap, spending alerts, easy key revocation. No shared user datastore. Worst case = token drain.
* Evaluation
  * Evaluation results will be recorded in Roam
    * user will copy and paste from the app and manually add feedback
    * can use <issue id="951383f9-b49b-4248-a7f2-e716849b2b33" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1604/extraction-run-on-benchmark-papers-quality-documented">ENG-1604</issue> 
    * can use [\[\[ISS\]\] - Initial paper benchmark results from \[\[Project/AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes\]\]](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SNeqhmSBF>)

---

## 4. Milestones

[M0: Architecture + Contracts](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-be0f7fd4-3db1-4680-8579-503ade3a900f>)

> **Deliverable:** Agreed extracted node schema, nodeType schema, PDF parser choice (LLM), and confirmation of layer boundaries. **Acceptance:** Interfaces reviewed; prompt/parser/model swappable without frontend redesign. **Dependencies:** None.

[M1: API route setup + Default Prompt](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e480b1cb-bd25-4e21-a0f8-c569806967a5>)

> **Deliverable:** API route + settings and returns normalized extracted nodes. **Acceptance:** Sample paper processed end-to-end; each extracted includes tag, content, and support reference; works on 2-3 benchmark papers; prompt includes few-shot examples. **Dependencies:** M0; node-type set from Matt/Joel; baseline prompt.

<linear-comment id="7b40b257-b525-434a-adb9-69b69a57c69b" resolved="false">[M2: Frontend App](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e8677cd6-0a74-4a87-a0c2-664b0a3d49a8>)</linear-comment>

> **Deliverable:** Page on discoursegraphs.com — upload, configure, run, review, select, copy. **Acceptance:** User completes full flow in browser; blocks render clearly; clipboard works. **Dependencies:** Stable M1 output schema.

[M3: Evaluation Baseline](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-171e0e29-3097-49b2-a508-aaa2a6785b18>)

> **Deliverable:** Manual evaluation — extraction run on benchmark papers, quality documented. **Acceptance:** Joel and Matt each evaluate 2-3 papers against known graphs; observations in Roam; obvious quality gaps identified. **Dependencies:** M1 stable; benchmark papers available.

### [M4: Smoke Test + Review + Merge ](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-8aca861c-37fa-4607-b2cd-93cd867b41cf>)

> **Deliverable:** Team review of full flow, decision log, merge to main. **Acceptance:** 10-min smoke test; axis-specific feedback on extraction quality, taxonomy, UX; merged and accessible. **Dependencies:** M2, M3.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

### P0 — Must have

FR0 - <issue id="9b44a383-68ca-463a-b097-764223f6072a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1601">ENG-1601</issue>

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| FR1 | <issue id="287e58ad-2246-4484-ac8d-5f28f603325a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1592">ENG-1592</issue> |
| FR2 | <issue id="171b2065-a196-4c0f-8487-26215b8a4921" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1593">ENG-1593</issue> |
| FR3 | <issue id="ea927329-04f6-4a02-9bcb-fd88031cd343" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1594">ENG-1594</issue> |
| FR4 | <issue id="e04c6495-d75c-42a8-af3d-d08959155e1d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1602/api-to-send-uploaded-pdf-to-chosen-llms-to-parse-from-fr1">ENG-1602</issue>, uses FR6 prompt |
| FR5 | ~~Chunk by section where boundaries are detectable (Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion)~~ using llm parser, will be included in FR6 prompt |
| FR6 | <issue id="089a3b0d-2d3e-42f8-b1a4-117b137fc3c6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1595">ENG-1595</issue> |
| FR7 | Each extracted node includes: node type tag, node content, supporting quote or figure/table reference |
| FR8 | <issue id="7829f53b-e3c4-4e62-81b9-668b52be05c8" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1596">ENG-1596</issue> |
| FR9 | <issue id="675ea294-3530-40e0-bfd4-aed017be1037" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1597">ENG-1597</issue> |
| FR10 | <issue id="d2fb1278-5075-424e-b13f-1e44cc23fe01" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1598">ENG-1598</issue> |

### 5.5  Non-Functional

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| NFR1 | <linear-comment id="592cad65-4129-4ab8-9a06-301ac26221f6" resolved="true">Support references include enough location info for quick re-finding in the paper</linear-comment> |
| NFR2 | <linear-comment id="26d54b85-b754-4d37-8d5c-ef96c94c610b" resolved="true">Reasonable defaults so a first-time user completes the flow without setup</linear-comment> |

---

## 6. Open Questions + Risks

### Open Questions

| \# | Question |
| -- | -- |
| 2 | <linear-comment id="ec7498b7-673d-485a-89d2-bc9671281e34" resolved="true">What does the clipboard output format look like? Should it match the graph's `[[CLM]] - {content}` format?</linear-comment> |
| 3 | Which few-shot examples should the prompt include, and from which papers? |
| 4 | What size or runtime limits on uploaded PDFs? |
| 5 | LLM model choice for extraction — cost vs. quality vs. context window? |
| 6 | Should the new `FLO` and `ART` discourse nodes be created before or after M0? |
| 7 | <linear-comment id="f6dd60e1-5543-463e-9194-713966bd8f0d" resolved="true">What fields belong in the extracted node schema to support future persistence without over-engineering MVP-0?</linear-comment> |

### Risks

| Risk | Impact |
| -- | -- |
| PDF extraction quality varies across publishers and scan quality | Weak input → weak extracted nodes |
| Figure/table-heavy papers may produce weak support references | Poor verifiability for certain paper types |
| Single broad prompt may over- or under-extract depending on paper structure | Inconsistent output quality |
| Public endpoint introduces token-abuse risk if spending limits are too loose | Cost blowout |
| If the review UI doesn't make verification easy, feedback quality will be poor even if extraction is reasonable | Team learning bottleneck |
| LLM PDF extraction might be a black box | Unable to inspect what text/content was actually extracted |
| LLM PDF extraction uses vision model | Which costs more |

---

{"id":"P-PRO-189","uuid":"fee500c3-2209-499a-8bd5-909f666deb57","icon":null,"color":"#f7c8c1","name":"Create DG MCP function library","summary":"","description":"[View in Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs//page/rgl9GMJe4>)

Starting with Roam:

Each ported function will be its own monorepo PR via `extensionAPI.ai.addTool` (25-tool cap per extension; per-tool scope read | append | edit).

**Status 2026-09-15: 34 functions now exist, verified, on [dg-team-mcp](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/dg-team-mcp>)** `main` **(15 discourse tools + 19 canvas tools).** The 26-function core completed with `get_candidate_nodes` (PR #14). PR #15 (<issue id="cd37120c-a0e4-4828-b77b-ab7bd1128910" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2276/canvas-mcp-nested-sub-canvas-portals-and-content-primitives">ENG-2276</issue>, merged the same day) added 8 canvas tools: tldraw-page create/rename/delete inside one canvas, nested sub-canvas portals (`canvas_add_subpage` / `canvas_link_subpage`, sharing the geo-plus-meta contract with <issue id="b0cdc4c8-3f9d-4944-a6ac-a3aa7c44b7b3" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2150/nested-pages-in-tldraw-canvas">ENG-2150</issue>'s plugin PR so every deployed client still loads the board), and geo/arrow/image authoring. `canvas_move` now moves shapes between tldraw pages, and the label-bearing tools take a `size`. The prototype library lives separate from the monorepo; the remaining core work is the monorepo port itself, not yet started. The Accepted / Maybe / Backburner sections below are candidates beyond these; none have code yet except relation retraction, whose `deleteStoredRelation` primitive exists internally but is unexposed. Note that 34 is nine OVER addTool's 25-tool per-extension cap, so the consolidations proposed in the table comments are required at port time, no longer optional. The canvas_dg_add / canvas_add collapse now carries most of the reduction: it covers the eight shape-authoring tools (node, block, connect, text, frame, geo, arrow, image). The get_node + get_node_section + batch get_nodes merge and folding get_candidate_nodes into get_all_discourse_nodes recover the rest.

## Ready

| Function | What it does | Existing code | Context | Comments |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **initial** |  |  |  |  |

Starting with Roam:

Each ported function will be its own monorepo PR via `extensionAPI.ai.addTool` (25-tool cap per extension; per-tool scope read | append | edit).

**Status 2026-09-15: 34 functions now exist, verified, on [dg-team-mcp](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/dg-team-mcp>)** `main` **(15 discourse tools + 19 canvas tools).** The 26-function core completed with `get_candidate_nodes` (PR #14). PR #15 (<issue id="cd37120c-a0e4-4828-b77b-ab7bd1128910" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2276/canvas-mcp-nested-sub-canvas-portals-and-content-primitives">ENG-2276</issue>, merged the same day) added 8 canvas tools: tldraw-page create/rename/delete inside one canvas, nested sub-canvas portals (`canvas_add_subpage` / `canvas_link_subpage`, sharing the geo-plus-meta contract with <issue id="b0cdc4c8-3f9d-4944-a6ac-a3aa7c44b7b3" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2150/nested-pages-in-tldraw-canvas">ENG-2150</issue>'s plugin PR so every deployed client still loads the board), and geo/arrow/image authoring. `canvas_move` now moves shapes between tldraw pages, and the label-bearing tools take a `size`. The prototype library lives separate from the monorepo; the remaining core work is the monorepo port itself, not yet started. The Accepted / Maybe / Backburner sections below are candidates beyond these; none have code yet except relation retraction, whose `deleteStoredRelation` primitive exists internally but is unexposed. Note that 34 is nine OVER addTool's 25-tool per-extension cap, so the consolidations proposed in the table comments are required at port time, no longer optional. The canvas_dg_add / canvas_add collapse now carries most of the reduction: it covers the eight shape-authoring tools (node, block, connect, text, frame, geo, arrow, image). The get_node + get_node_section + batch get_nodes merge and folding get_candidate_nodes into get_all_discourse_nodes recover the rest.

3. Ability to share link to node

content.text:
I found about 20 projects affected by DG accounts. Seven of them used the space account as a stand-in for personal accounts. My method has limits: I read every project's name and summary, searched issues for "space account" and "anonymous", and read about ten issues and projects closely. I did not go through every issue in every project.

## The accounts project itself

**Discourse Graph Accounts (P-DIS-83, Accepted)**
- The done tickets are the graph-based "Quick for Beta" path: ENG-418, 420, 423, 424, 567, 589.
- The personal-account tickets are still in Backlog: ENG-373, 405, 419, 421, 422, 918, 1511.
- **Review:** the project description and those tickets come before the Roam spec (H3a0tja8D). For example, ENG-421 assumes login happens in each frontend, but the spec leans toward login always on the Website with OAuth 2.1. Reconcile the two once the spec settles.

## Past projects that used space accounts as a workaround

**Obsidian within-lab collaboration (P-DES-133, In Progress)**
- ENG-1177 authenticates a vault as a space pseudo-user.
- ENG-1179, 1232 and 1238 build groups whose members are space pseudo-users.
- ENG-1650 is a "temporary username": it sets the name on the vault's pseudo-user and lists DG accounts as out of scope.
- ENG-2122 (Triage): if the plugin's stored password is lost, the vault loses database access, and there is no way to recover it. The ticket says a recovery path "would require DiscourseGraph accounts".
- **Review:**
  - Should the temporary username become a profile name?
  - Does ENG-2122 wait for accounts or get its own fix?
  - Do group members stay spaces?

**Sharing group management (P-ENG-170, Completed)**
- ENG-1703 opens the Website with the space's session token in the URL. The ticket says plainly that this stands in for cookie login with personal accounts.
- ENG-1702 (invite) and ENG-1723 (list members) both work on spaces.
- **Review:** this is the clearest migration case.
  - The Website login becomes personal.
  - Group admin rights would come through the `self_to_spaces()` set in the spec.
  - Decide whether you invite a person or a space.

**Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian (P-DIS-166, In Progress)**
- All publishing and importing runs under the space session.
- ENG-2298 fixed an import panel that named a Roam space after one of its authors.
- ENG-2344, 2359 and 2368 tune the `my_*` access views, which are keyed on the space identity.
- ENG-2335 checks group publication for imported nodes.
- **Review:**
  - The access views get rewritten on the `self_to_*` sets, and the RLS performance work has to be redone for them.
  - Decide how author and space names appear once profile names exist.

**KOI for knowledge interop (P-ENG-164, Backlog)**
- ENG-1837 adds the "everyone" pseudo-user.
- ENG-1674 and 1675 document the API, including space creation.
- **Review:** in the spec, `my_identity_accounts()` is to be renamed `self_to_groups()` before ENG-1837 merges. Hold the API docs until the auth model is known, or document the space flow as interim.

**Infrastructure for Embeddings (P-ENG-75, Icebox)**
- ENG-417 revised the alpha functions for the graph accounts.
- ENG-1835 ("search scoped to current space") was canceled.
- ENG-982 dealt with duplicate spaces for the browser and the desktop app.
- **Review:** low priority. Revisit search scope when semantic search comes back.

**Not checked, likely affected:**
- *Real-time tldraw collaboration (P-FEE-149, In Progress):* its scope includes "who is allowed to use real-time sync, how access is granted and revoked". I didn't check whether that relies on graph membership or on the space session.
- *Create Initial Admin Panel (P-ENG-106, Completed):* a hidden panel in the Roam settings. Worth a look to see which session it uses.

## Current or planned projects that depend on accounts

**Cross-space search**
- Projects:
  - *Search and filter nodes from other spaces in advanced node search (P-ENG-192, Planning):* it says "any space the user is a member of". Today that membership is per space, not per person.
  - *Roam: Initial advanced search (P-DIS-79):* the summary says "eventually cross graph search".
- **Review:** this is the first place a person must see how they are logged in (see the spec's UX touchpoints section). Scope P-ENG-192 so its first version doesn't hard-code space-only reach.

**Share and import to/from web (P-PRO-183, Proposal)**
- It names Discourse Graph Accounts as a requirement.

**Headless DG retrieval API and MCP from database (P-DIS-186)**
- Agents reading the database need an identity. This is the agent and agent_grant part of the spec.

**Create DG MCP function library (P-PRO-189)**
- It runs on the Roam side today and uses `tokenUserUid` for write attribution.
- "Multi-graph search" is on its backburner list and would need accounts.

**AI-assisted extraction (P-DIS-140)**
- "Full auth or multi-user accounts" is out of scope for MVP-0, and the project lists token abuse as a risk.
- Any persistence later needs accounts. The ENG-1999 audit of API route abuse is related.

**Website and inter-graph projects** (each needs either a Website login or a multi-space identity):
- DG tldraw web (P-ENG-176)
- TLdraw sync between graphs (P-DIS-153)
- Push and pull between two Roam graphs (P-DIS-165)
- Post-V0 sync architecture (P-ENG-185)

## How to review them

For each past project, I'd ask three questions:
1. **Which identity does it act as?** Today that is always the space session. Ask whether it should become the person, stay the space, or allow both. The spec's two-session model (personal for reads, search and acting as the person; space for sync, groups and sharing) answers most cases.
2. **Did it leave anything visible to users that accounts would change?** Examples: usernames, the token-in-URL Website login, groups made of spaces, the password-loss dead end.
3. **Migrate, keep, or retire?**
   - Migrate: ENG-1703's Website login, the `my_*` views.
   - Keep as the space path: the sync credentials.
   - Retire: the temporary username, once profile names exist.

A practical way to do it would be a section on the spec page that lists these projects with the answer to each question. You could also tag the affected issues with a Linear label, but I haven't created anything. I can add that section to the Roam page if you want.

Exploration of personal accounts (Linear project "Discourse Graph Accounts", Roam project page Tow9ZlFAi). The working document is Roam page "Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts" (H3a0tja8D). I write there directly, and only there. It maps options with costs for the group; the user does not want premature decisions, and decisions in older notes are not settled.

Decided or strong leanings, as of 2026-10-23:
- Cross-space search inside the platforms; `Website` joins the `Platform` enum; password accounts stay; no forcing Roam users to sign up; Roam API tokens need a subscription, so token-based proof is never required.
- A person reaches a space only through a claimed PlatformAccount (A, B and any direct person-to-space edge ruled out). Preferred: claim reach scoped by attestation (`asserted` reaches only the vouching space).
- No group nesting or recursive queries; no database-level invites into spaces; close the `group_membership` insert hole first.
- Space admin = flag plus level on `LocalAccess`: guessed < registered < proven, each with a delegated level just below it; delegates can name same-level delegates; demotion only of strictly lower levels, manual, through an admin UI; the delegator is not recorded. Admins approving identity claims is set aside.
- Admin can prove with a backend token, discarded or stored (stored is an explicit opt-in, and enables L6 for the whole graph).
- Emails stored but hidden until shared; names are shown as name plus PlatformAccount id. Profile visibility: one row per person and audience with an array of fields.
- Two sessions in the plugin: personal for reads, search and actions as the person; space for sync, groups and sharing. Personal session delivery: Supabase Auth as OAuth 2.1 server (plugin is a PKCE client; login always on the Website; MAU cost accepted; completing inside the plugin is nice to have, with a `secret_token` fallback). Social login is for adding identities and logging in on the Website. A claimed account shows the profile name.

- Access resolution: three nested sets `self_to_spaces()` (group membership/admin checks), `self_to_groups()` (sharing checks), `self_to_everyone()` (reads), replacing `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. A person acting for S is admin of G when S is (stage 1); stage 2 restricts that to admins of S. Sets return a cap per uid; the initplan RLS rewrite is a prerequisite.

Verified 2026-10-24: Roam clients can't forge `:create/user` (no `roamDatomicAlphaAPI`); only graph owners/admins create backend tokens; Obsidian account ids are per vault (vault name + random suffix, synced with the vault); ORCID can be a Supabase custom OIDC provider (identity linking and `email_optional` still to check); ATProto likely needs its own flow (untested).

New layer L8: Roam's Firebase ID token (IndexedDB `firebaseLocalStorageDb`, issuer `securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`, `sub` = Roam uid, verified email) can be checked server-side. Works in the desktop app and in browsers. Blocked until Roam's ToS is checked and Roam agrees.

Open: identity-link package (L0–L8, the group's call); Roam token storage pending (memory and a click per reload vs refresh token in `localStorage`); lease length; whether the backend API returns `:user/email`; whether imports keep creator and timestamps; whether the OAuth flow completes inside the plugins. Latent bug: `upsert_account_in_space` copies `SpaceAccess` once `dg_account` is set. ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()` should be renamed `self_to_groups()` before it merges.

Answered 2026-10-26: `roamAlphaAPI.user.isAdmin` (synchronous, no parameters, current user only; docs say "admin of this graph (the graph owner)", so whether non-owner admins count is unclear). Recorded under Space admin → Guessed (block SdqDeXOxt): it makes the Roam guess correct but no harder to forge, since it is sent under the space session.
